item.title: Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb is seeking revenge on Cardinals in Week 8 after massive losing streak
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb is seeking revenge on Cardinals in Week 8 after massive losing streak appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It seems like the rumors are flying around George Pickens and the Dallas Cowboys . But what’s next is the matchup against the Cardinals . And CeeDee Lamb is seeking revenge on the Cardinals in Week 8 after a losing streak , according to a post on X by Todd Archer. “CeeDee Lamb was asked about a ‘heightened awareness’ this week for the Cowboys because Arizona beat them last year. ‘I’ve never beat the Cardinals since I’ve been in the league, so that’s kind of fair to say,’ Lamb said.’I wouldn’t say heightened focus, but it’s definitely another take.’ ” What’s up with the Cowboys losing to the lowly Cardinals? Arizona has won four straight (2020, ’22, ’23 and ’25) and three have been at AT&T Stadium. Lamb said the Cardinals have been a different bunch when they play the Cowboys. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “They’ve always had more energy,” Lamb said. “Just coming out in the game, they’re more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o’clock, Sunday night, Monday night. We played them in primetime. They beat us there. So just coming in, treating them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be, you know what I’m saying? So hats off to them in their prep. And we just got to go match them, if not overpower them.” Uh, the Cardinals may be a Super Bowl-contending team? Seriously? Why do the Cowboys need to invent fake narratives to get themselves fired up for an NFL game? Weird stuff. One good thing for the Cowboys is they are coming off an impressive offensive performance — even if it was against a team that looked mailed in over the last 15-20 minutes. Lamb said the Cowboys rediscovered their identity , according to dallascowboys.com. “No, that’s exactly who we are. We’re better balanced,” he said. “We could beat you in a run game. We could beat you in the pass [game].” Individually, Lamb says defenses cannot guard him. “I think my ability to line up anywhere in the offense and run any route on the route tree,” Lamb said. “I feel like I could (beat) anybody in front of me, and I’m standing on that.” Related: Cowboys rumors: Is George Pickens trade a serious possibility after Brian Schottenheimer callout? Related: Giving up 2 catches this season has Cowboys’ Joey Porter Jr. ‘pissed’

item.title: Columbus Blue Jackets come up short against Carolina Hurricanes
item.description: They finished strong in a road matchup against the reigning Stanley Cup champions, but the Blue Jackets couldn't overcome a three-goal deficit in a 3-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 29 in Raleigh, North Carolina. More: Cam Talbot continues to shine in Columbus Blue Jackets' OT win Denton Mateychuk and Kent Johnson scored goals 2:54 apart to pull the Blue Jackets (5-6-0) within 3-2 in the third period, but Mark Jankowski's goal for Carolina 16 seconds into the period was the difference. Hurricanes goalie Pyotr Kochetkov (24 saves) didn't allow another goal despite the Jackets pushing late with their net empty for a 6-on-5 advantage. Mateychuk cut it to 3-1 at 6:56 of the third to extend his goal streak to three straight games and Johnson followed by capping a power play at 9:50 for his seventh goal of the season. There just wasn't a tying goal in the cards for the Blue Jackets, who got 24 saves from goalie Jet Greaves in his first game since taking the loss Oct. 20 against the Toronto Maple Leafs . Jordan Martinook and Logan Stankoven scored the first two goals for the Hurricanes (11-2-2), who've won four of their past five games and sit comfortably atop the Metropolitan Division with 24 points and a cushion of eight points over the New Jersey Devils in second. The Blue Jackets will wrap up their first multi-game road trip of the season Oct. 31 in Dallas. Dispatch Blue Jackets/Crew reporter Brian Hedger can be reached at bhedger@dispatch.com This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Columbus Blue Jackets come up short against Carolina Hurricanes

item.title: Panthers vs Packers: TNF first half recap
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images First Quarter A forced and recovered fumble on the opening kickoff earned the Panthers the ball to start the game and their first turnover in three games. Interior pressure buckled the opening drive before it got started and the Panthers had to settle for a field goal. The defenses traded three and outs from there until a big pass interference penalty opened things up for the Packers. A big pass against an unsuccessful big blitz followed that penalty and led to the Packers first TD. A missed extra point then kept the spirit of Panthers football alive. The Panthers stretched the perimeter of the field to move away from the interior pressure and into the red zone after, getting to a 4th and 1 with 1:00 left in the first quarter. Chuba Hubbard ran for a hard one yard, showing success where the panthers have struggled in short yardsge. The next play he carried them to the 1 yard line and the end of the 1st quarter. Second Quarter Hubbard punched it in on second and goal to start the wuarter and regain a Panthers lead A second Green Bay fumble on ensuing drive gave the Panthers a big opportunity to expand their lead. Unfortunately, their offensive line did their best impression of tissue paper and the Panthers punted after three plays. Packers game plan seems to be attempting therapy for their running game. So far so therapeutic for the Panthers run defense. Unfortunately, less could be said for the pass defense. A deep bomb surrendered to Christian Watson led to both him and Will Lee III leaving the game with injuries. Chau Smith-Wade and Marco Wilson were the corners left standing. Somehow, the defense held the Packers until third and goal from the one, but Josh Jacobs found plenty of room for a score at the end of the drive to retake a Packers lead. The Panthers started their second possession of the second quarter with 6:28 left on the clock. A Green Bay penalty on third and eight turned into a tipped pass for an interception on third and three. Green Bay ended up with the football at the 48 yard line with 5:18 left in the half. Quick, short passes moved the Packers safely down the field. The occasional running play allowed the Panthers defense to flash competence, but the Packers leaned on the pass as needed to score a touchdown that felt inevitable. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images First Quarter A forced and recovered fumble on the opening kickoff earned the Panthers the ball to start the game and their first turnover in three games. Second Quarter Hubbard punched it in on second and goal to start the wuarter and regain a Panthers lead A second Green Bay fumble on ensuing drive gave the Panthers a big opportunity to expand their lead. Unfortunately, their offensive line did their best impression of tissue paper and the Panthers punted after three plays. Packers game plan seems to be attempting therapy for their running game. So far so therapeutic for the Panthers run defense. Unfortunately, less could be said for the pass defense. A deep bomb surrendered to Christian Watson led to both him and Will Lee III leaving the game with injuries. Chau Smith-Wade and Marco Wilson were the corners left standing. Somehow, the defense held the Packers until third and goal from the one, but Josh Jacobs found plenty of room for a score at the end of the drive to retake a Packers lead. The Panthers started their second possession of the second quarter with 6:28 left on the clock. A Green Bay penalty on third and eight turned into a tipped pass for an interception on third and three. Green Bay ended up with the football at the 48 yard line with 5:18 left in the half. Quick, short passes moved the Packers safely down the field. The occasional running play allowed the Panthers defense to flash competence, but the Packers leaned on the pass as needed to score a touchdown that felt inevitable. Inside of two minutes left in the half, it felt like the Panthers were out of answers in their secondary. Edge pressure and bad offensive tackle play killed the two-minute drill and the Panthers went in to the half with what had been a one possession game feeling increasingly out of reach. Half Time The Panthers were firing on zero cylinders in the first half. Injuries have exposed paper thin depth along both fronts. Young had no time to throw, highlighted by Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker combining in the first half for one reception on five targets. Meanwhile, the defense couldn’t cover, couldn’t pressure, and thus couldn’t get the Packers off the field when they needed to. Writing this at halftime, I expect the second half to be long and unsatisfying to watch as a Panthers fan. Third Quarter

item.title: Luka Doncic cleared for injury return in Warriors clash
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Luka Doncic cleared for injury return in Warriors clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After being sidelined against the LA Clippers due to a back issue , Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic was off the team’s injury report ahead of their upcoming game on the road against the Golden State Warriors on Friday. Prior to Wednesday’s win against the Clippers, Lakers head coach JJ Redick acknowledged that Doncic’s status was nothing overly concerning, just precautionary as the team heads into a stretch of five games in seven nights. In addition to Luka Doncic, the Lakers might get forward Ziaire Williams back from injury as he was listed as questionable against the Warriors. Williams also was ruled out against the Clippers in similar precaution. The sixth-year wing signed with the Lakers in the offseason via free agency, and has been among the team’s most consistent players to this point as a starting forward. With Doncic back in the lineup, however, the on-court antics are certainly going to draw headlines as much, if not more, than the actual basketball. During the Lakers’ season opening win against the Warriors back on Oct. 21, Doncic was engaged in a trash-talking battle with Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg . Doncic got the better of that matchup, which included burying a half-court bomb to beat the halftime buzzer. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After the game, both players acknowledged the chatter throughout the game, but Lendeborg took it a step further, proclaiming he had lost respect for Doncic due to his perceived complaining to the officials. Lendeborg was hit with a technical foul during the game, with teammate Draymond Green coming to his defense about. For the Lakers, the return of their star player is a much welcome development. The Slovenian native has gotten off to a blistering start to the season, and is among the early MVP candidates. He dropped a season-high 52 points last Sunday to help the Lakers grab a come-from-behind win against the Utah Jazz, and he followed that up with a 41-point effort despite a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. Across the first four games of the season, Doncic is averaging a league-leading 36.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.3 steals with splits of 48.4 percent shooting from the field, 39.6 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 87.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. He is also currently leading the league in 3-point shots made and attempted, and free-throws attempted. Related: Ziaire Williams does not stutter over NBA flopping crackdown Related: Lakers’ Collin Sexton shares intense mindset behind huge game vs. Clippers

item.title: UFC BJJ 13 live stream, results, video highlights | New champ to take Musumeci’s belt
item.description: UFC BJJ 13 happens on THURSDAY (October 29, 2026) inside the UFC’s Meta Apex venue in Las Vegas, Nevada. The event will be topped by two title bouts, and will also feature CJI and ADCC champions returning to the promotion. Mikey Musumeci ’s belt will soon have a new owner after the first and only UFC BJJ bantamweight champion has decided to relinquish his title to “prioritize MMA training” and fun jiu-jitsu matches as he ends his “serious” grappling career . Competing for the now vacant belt is Musumeci’s training partner and two-time world champion Jalen Fonacier , with the Filipino-American grappler taking on Kleber Barboza . That bout will be on the co-main event, with the actual headliner being another vacant title bout featuring Jay Rodriguez and William Tackett , who will receive his second shot at a UFC BJJ belt. Jay’s more popular brother and CJI champ Nick Rodriguez will also be on the stacked card against recent IBJJF Pan-Am champ Nata Tenca . The stacked card also features reigning and former ADCC champions’ returns, with Jasmine Rocha and Ffion Davies being on separate bouts. CJI vet and champion wrestler Pat Downey also makes his debut on the deep UFC BJJ 13 line up. The no gi Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) event will stream LIVE on UFC Fight Pass, starting at 8 p.m. ET . Join us below for live results, and highlights from UFC BJJ 13. UFC BJJ 13 free live stream Unfortunately, the entire card will no longer be free on YouTube like their earlier events, but a free live stream of the earlier matches will be available again and embedded below. item.title: Lexington can't overcome slow start, falls in Division III district final
item.description: LEXINGTON — The Lexington Lady Lex found out the hard way the importance of starting soccer games off the right way. In their 2-1 Division III district championship loss to Elida on Thursday, Oct. 29, Lady Lex experienced a slow start and took a little too long to get things going. The loss ended their season with a 13-4-3 record. “I felt like we played with a lot of nerves,” Lexington coach Buck Morton said. “We never got the ball down to our feet. We knew that this would be a different level of game just from watching them on film and seeing that they moved more athletically and played with physicality. We knew it would be a tough game, but we had to play through not great touches.” KEEP UP WITH THE POSTSEASON: 2026 fall sports postseason tracker | Clear Fork wins girls soccer program's 10th district title Elida scored the opening goal off of a corner kick with 27:06 remaining in the first half and the score stood 1-0 into halftime. Lexington sophomore Jersie Palmer evened things up with 30:21 remaining when she rebounded a Morgan Harrod shot that drilled the post and bounced perfectly back to Palmer who finished the goal. Lady Lex saw two more shots go off the cross bar and one more off the post as they were literally inches away from taking the lead multiple times. “We gave up a really soft goal on the cross. Any number of girls could have redirected that, but those things happen,” Morton said. “When we settled in and did what we have done all year long as a second-half team, we came back had three really close calls on potential goals.” Elida took the lead for good with 18:22 remaining when Lexington was called for a late foul in the box. Lexie Good drilled the penalty kick to the upper 90 and gave Elida the lead and eventually the win. “I just didn’t agree with the call,” Morton said. “The ball was clearly away and nothing like that was called all night long and it was awarded with a PK. I didn’t agree with that at all. We came down and the girl basically catches the ball at the end of the game, and we had almost the same thing happen on our end and the reason for no call was because the ball was away. We already set that standard, so I will have to watch it again and maybe I’ll see it differently. “I am not putting the blame there. We have to take care of what we need to take care of in the end, but I do thing that it was more than unfortunate that it came down like that.” Lexington finishes as the Division III district runner-up and will say goodbye to six seniors, Claire Hammer, Emilee VanGilder, Morgan Harrod, Hayley Walker, Carliann Hughes and Gabby Lay. “At the end of the year, you look back on the good and the bad and I will always see this team as one of the most connected I have ever coached,” Morton said. “Our senior class is great and we will miss every one of them because they were always all about the game and the team. Any number of girls could have redirected that, but those things happen,” Morton said. “When we settled in and did what we have done all year long as a second-half team, we came back had three really close calls on potential goals.” Elida took the lead for good with 18:22 remaining when Lexington was called for a late foul in the box. Lexie Good drilled the penalty kick to the upper 90 and gave Elida the lead and eventually the win. “I just didn’t agree with the call,” Morton said. “The ball was clearly away and nothing like that was called all night long and it was awarded with a PK. I didn’t agree with that at all. We came down and the girl basically catches the ball at the end of the game, and we had almost the same thing happen on our end and the reason for no call was because the ball was away. We already set that standard, so I will have to watch it again and maybe I’ll see it differently. “I am not putting the blame there. We have to take care of what we need to take care of in the end, but I do thing that it was more than unfortunate that it came down like that.” Lexington finishes as the Division III district runner-up and will say goodbye to six seniors, Claire Hammer, Emilee VanGilder, Morgan Harrod, Hayley Walker, Carliann Hughes and Gabby Lay. “At the end of the year, you look back on the good and the bad and I will always see this team as one of the most connected I have ever coached,” Morton said. “Our senior class is great and we will miss every one of them because they were always all about the game and the team. They embraced the idea that we preach as a coaching staff that everyone has to play every game like it is their senior year and buy in because you never know what is going to be next. This senior class had done that.” This article originally appeared on Mansfield News Journal: Lexington can't overcome slow start, falls in Division III district final

item.title: Howie Roseman takes another Jalen Carter-like swing in latest ClutchPoints’ 2027 NFL Mock Draft
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Howie Roseman takes another Jalen Carter-like swing in latest ClutchPoints’ 2027 NFL Mock Draft appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles could be heading toward a much different offseason than expected. After a difficult start to the 2026 NFL season , injuries and consecutive losses have raised questions about the team’s ability to turn things around. With the possibility of an early first-round selection becoming more realistic, Roseman could have an opportunity to address one of the Eagles roster’s biggest needs in the 2027 NFL Draft. In the latest ClutchPoints 2027 NFL Mock Draft, Philadelphia selects South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart, a prospect who could provide a significant boost to its pass rush. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Stewart has the physical tools and athleticism to become one of the most dangerous edge defenders in his draft class. His potential is undeniable, but concerns about his decision-making on and off the field could cause him to slide down the first round. He was also suspended for one game following an incident against Alabama, adding to the questions surrounding his draft stock. That could put the Eagles in an interesting position. Despite investing heavily in their defense, Philadelphia could still use another disruptive pass rusher to complement its existing talent. Stewart’s upside makes him an appealing option, particularly if he remains available later than expected. The projected move also brings back memories of the 2023 NFL Draft , when Roseman traded up to select Jalen Carter despite concerns surrounding the defensive tackle’s pre-draft situation. Carter eventually became a cornerstone of Philadelphia’s defense, making that gamble worthwhile. Roseman has already shown that he is willing to take this kind of gamble when the talent is too good to pass up. His decision to bring Carter to Philadelphia paid off, and Stewart could give the Eagles another opportunity to land a defensive difference-maker. Whether Roseman is willing to take that same risk again remains to be seen, but the potential reward could be exactly what Philadelphia needs. Related: Cloud grows around Eagles RB Saquon Barkley’s Week 8 availability after latest injury update Related: Eagles rumors: Why Tom Pelissero isn’t ruling out Howie Roseman being a trade deadline buyer

item.title: Panthers start TNF on fire by forcing kickoff fumble vs. Packers
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Panthers start TNF on fire by forcing kickoff fumble vs. Packers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Carolina Panthers faced a defensive dilemma before facing the Green Bay Packers . But set the tone on special teams during their road trip to Lambeau Field. Jackson Kuwatch and Nick Hampton became responsible for igniting the Panthers’ side early. Coleman Owen retrieved the opening kickoff from his own eight-yard line. Owen fielded it back to the 27-yard line, but lost control of the football on this Kuwatch hit. WHAT A START TO TNF 🍿 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Panthers force the Packers fumble on the opening kickoff and RECOVER! pic.twitter.com/kWBsS08fXK — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 30, 2026 Hampton became the defender on the spot to pounce on the loose football. It marks the first time this season that the Panthers recovered the opening kickoff. Plus also becomes the first fumble recovery by the Panthers’ special teams unit this season. Carolina and quarterback Bryce Young were handed a very short field to work with. Coach Dave Canales kept things simple in that sequence, trusting the ground attack with three running plays. Young, though, took a costly sack by Devonte Wyatt on third down. The Panthers settled for the field goal in completing the six-play, eight-yard drive following the fumble recovery to go up 3-0. Carolina walked into the historic NFL venue with a 3-3 overall record. But are fresh off receiving a rough 43-13 defeat at the hands of the fierce NFC South rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers from Sunday. The loss became the most one-sided defeat this season for Canales and the Panthers. Carolina struggled to move the ball during its second possession, going three-and-out and sending the punt team out. Then Packers quarterback Jordan Love found tight end Tucker Kraft for a 12-yard red zone touchdown to place GB up 6-3. Related: Panthers elevate Cardinals draftee for TNF amid cornerback injury crisis Related: Panthers’ Jaelan Phillips gets injury update for Packers TNF game

item.title: Valkyries will add to Bay Area's epic Game 7 history, filled with glory and heartbreak
item.description: Left: The San Francisco Giants' Madison Bumgarner and Buster Posey embrace after winning Game 7 of the 2014 World Series in Kansas City. Center: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry watches the Cleveland Cavaliers celebrate after Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals at Oracle Arena. Right: The San Jose Sharks' Tomas Hertl leaps with joy after scoring a goal against the Colorado Avalanche in Game 7 of the 2019 Western Conference second round. (Scott Strazzante/S.F. Chronicle, Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle, Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) One compelling reason the words "Game 7" stir the sports fan's soul: It seldom happens. Only six times in Bay Area history has a local franchise played in Game 7 with the championship at stake. And only three times has that captivating, tension-filled, winner-take-all event taken place here: Giants-Yankees in the 1962 World Series, A's-Mets in the 1973 World Series and Warriors-Cavaliers in the 2016 NBA Finals. Now we have a fourth entry. Saturday's Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center, featuring the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream, counts as a milestone on multiple levels. It also will mark the first time a WNBA postseason series has reached Game 7 - the league adopted a best-of-seven Finals format last year, when Las Vegas swept Phoenix. The previous year, in 2024, New York and Minnesota went the distance in their best-of-five Finals (the Liberty won 67-62 in Game 5). Any decisive game brings sporting theater, but Game 7s carry extra cachet - as the culmination of a long series, with sustained drama and wild momentum swings. That's exactly how this Valkyries-Dream duel has unfolded. Atlanta seemed in control after taking a 2-1 lead … and then Golden State stormed back to move ahead 3-2 … and then the Dream averted elimination with Thursday's emphatic victory. So now the series moves onto the grandest stage of all. Bay Area Game 7 history Saturday's showdown between the Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will be the 32nd time a Bay Area franchise has played in Game 7 of a postseason series - and only the seventh time it's happened with a championship at stake. Here's a rundown of the previous instances: 2025: Warriors win first round vs. Rockets, 103-89 2023: Warriors win first round vs. Kings, 120-100 2019: Sharks win West semifinals vs. Avalanche, 3-2 2019: Sharks win first round vs. Golden Knights, 5-4 (OT) 2018: Warriors win West finals vs. Rockets, 101-92 2016: Warriors lose NBA Finals vs. Cavaliers, 93-89 2016: Warriors win West finals vs. Thunder, 96-88 2016: Sharks win West semifinals vs. Predators, 5-0 2014: Giants win World Series vs. Royals, 3-2 2014: Warriors lose first round vs. Clippers, 126-121 2014: Sharks lose first round vs. Kings, 5-1 2013: Sharks lose West semifinals vs. Kings, 2-1 2012: Giants win NLCS vs. Cardinals, 9-0 2011: Sharks win West semifinals vs. Red Wings, 3-2 2008: Sharks win first round vs. Flames, 5-3 2002: Giants lose World Series vs. Angels, 4-1 2002: Sharks lo
item.content:encoded: Left: The San Francisco Giants' Madison Bumgarner and Buster Posey embrace after winning Game 7 of the 2014 World Series in Kansas City. Center: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry watches the Cleveland Cavaliers celebrate after Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals at Oracle Arena. Right: The San Jose Sharks' Tomas Hertl leaps with joy after scoring a goal against the Colorado Avalanche in Game 7 of the 2019 Western Conference second round. (Scott Strazzante/S.F. Chronicle, Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle, Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) One compelling reason the words "Game 7" stir the sports fan's soul: It seldom happens. Only six times in Bay Area history has a local franchise played in Game 7 with the championship at stake. And only three times has that captivating, tension-filled, winner-take-all event taken place here: Giants-Yankees in the 1962 World Series, A's-Mets in the 1973 World Series and Warriors-Cavaliers in the 2016 NBA Finals. Now we have a fourth entry. Saturday's Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center, featuring the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream, counts as a milestone on multiple levels. It also will mark the first time a WNBA postseason series has reached Game 7 - the league adopted a best-of-seven Finals format last year, when Las Vegas swept Phoenix. The previous year, in 2024, New York and Minnesota went the distance in their best-of-five Finals (the Liberty won 67-62 in Game 5). Any decisive game brings sporting theater, but Game 7s carry extra cachet - as the culmination of a long series, with sustained drama and wild momentum swings. That's exactly how this Valkyries-Dream duel has unfolded. Atlanta seemed in control after taking a 2-1 lead … and then Golden State stormed back to move ahead 3-2 … and then the Dream averted elimination with Thursday's emphatic victory. So now the series moves onto the grandest stage of all. Bay Area Game 7 history Saturday's showdown between the Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will be the 32nd time a Bay Area franchise has played in Game 7 of a postseason series - and only the seventh time it's happened with a championship at stake. Here's a rundown of the previous instances: 2025: Warriors win first round vs. Rockets, 103-89 2023: Warriors win first round vs. Kings, 120-100 2019: Sharks win West semifinals vs. Avalanche, 3-2 2019: Sharks win first round vs. Golden Knights, 5-4 (OT) 2018: Warriors win West finals vs. Rockets, 101-92 2016: Warriors lose NBA Finals vs. Cavaliers, 93-89 2016: Warriors win West finals vs. Thunder, 96-88 2016: Sharks win West semifinals vs. Predators, 5-0 2014: Giants win World Series vs. Royals, 3-2 2014: Warriors lose first round vs. Clippers, 126-121 2014: Sharks lose first round vs. Kings, 5-1 2013: Sharks lose West semifinals vs. Kings, 2-1 2012: Giants win NLCS vs. Cardinals, 9-0 2011: Sharks win West semifinals vs. Red Wings, 3-2 2008: Sharks win first round vs. Flames, 5-3 2002: Giants lose World Series vs. Angels, 4-1 2002: Sharks lose West semifinals vs. Avalanche, 1-0 2000: Sharks win first round vs. Blues, 3-1 1995: Sharks win first round vs. Flames, 5-4 1994: Sharks lose West semifinals vs. Maple Leafs, 4-2 1994: Sharks win first round vs. Red Wings, 3-2 1987: Giants lose NLCS vs. Cardinals, 6-0 1977: Warriors lose West semifinals vs. Lakers, 97-84 1976: Warriors lose West finals vs. Suns, 94-86 1975: Warriors win West finals vs. Bulls, 83-79 1973: A's win World Series vs. Mets, 5-2 1972: A's win World Series vs. Reds, 3-2 1969: Oakland Oaks (ABA) win West semifinals vs. Denver Rockets, 115-102 1969: Oakland Seals (NHL) lose first round vs. L.A. Kings, 5-3 1964: Warriors win West finals vs. St. Louis Hawks, 105-95 1962: Giants lose World Series vs. Yankees, 1-0 Consider the indelible memories Game 7s have produced for Bay Area fans, some dripping with joy and others soaked in frustration. Willie McCovey's lineout to end the '62 Series, with the tying run on third base and winning run on second. Madison Bumgarner's epic, five-inning save to beat Kansas City in the 2014 World Series. LeBron James' chase-down block in the '16 NBA Finals. Bumgarner closed out one of three championship-series Game 7s involving a Bay Area team but played on the road. The other two: A's-Reds in the 1972 World Series (Oakland won 3-2) and Giants-Angels in the 2002 World Series (Anaheim won 4-1). Widen the scope beyond the title series, and other Game 7s also yielded memorable feats. Stephen Curry dropped 50 points on the Kings in a first-round series in 2023 (two years later, Buddy Hield scored 33 to push the Warriors past Houston in the first round). The Sharks earned a one-goal Game 7 win in the first round of the 2019 Stanley Cup playoffs, then did the same in the West semifinals. Giants second baseman Marco Scutaro rejoiced in the rain just before the final out of the 2012 National League Championship Series. In all, Bay Area teams have played in Game 7 at any stage in the postseason just 31 times in the nearly seven decades since the Giants moved to San Francisco in 1958. The Sharks have played in the most (12), followed by the Warriors (10) - including six in the Curry Era - Giants (five), A's (two) and the ABA's Oakland Oaks and NHL's Oakland Seals (one each). Ten years ago, before the Warriors faced Oklahoma City in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals, the Chronicle explored this history . Golden State's journey showed how seldom Game 7s occur - the Warriors played in three of them in the mid-1970s, then not again until the 2014 first round against the Los Angeles Clippers (a five-point loss in Mark Jackson's last game as head coach). As they learned - and the Valkyries will find out Saturday - one play can propel a team to triumph or launch a lifetime of painful, "What if?" reflection. "Every possession is more intense, from tipoff to the last possession of the game," former Warriors forward Andre Iguodala said in an interview for the 2016 story. "Everything is kind of magnified. You can tell there are nerves, because no one wants to be at fault. So everyone is trying to make the correct play, the correct pass, the right reads. Every little thing counts." Iguodala played in one Game 7 with Philadelphia, an 85-75 loss to Boston in the 2012 Eastern Conference semifinals. He scored 18 points, but he also recalled botched defensive rotations that left Ray Allen and Paul Pierce open for jumpers. That's the thing about Game 7s: The memories linger longer and more vividly. Former Giants first baseman J.T. Snow recalled the raucous atmosphere at Anaheim Stadium for Game 7 of the 2002 World Series. Those were the days of the Rally Monkey mascot and fans banging Thunderstix, but Snow savored the setting even if the Giants lost. "It was probably more electric than any game I've ever played in my whole life," he said in 2016. "You could sense it everywhere, from the clubhouse to the field during batting practice. The whole season compresses down to those three hours and 27 outs. I loved it. I wish we had won, but it was fun." The Rick Barry-led Warriors lost two of those three Game 7s in the ‘70s, falling to Phoenix in the 1976 West finals and the Lakers in the '77 conference semifinals. Before that, Golden State bounced back from an 11-point halftime deficit to beat Chicago in Game 7 of the 1975 West finals (yes, the Bulls were in the West back then). The Warriors subsequently swept Washington to win the NBA title. More than 40 years later, Barry remembered the tension - and agonizing first half - of that Game 7 against the Bulls. "I remember stinking up the gym and sitting on the freaking bench, praying for my teammates to do well," he said in 2016. "They did, and held the Bulls scoreless for seven minutes. Thankfully, I came back in and made some shots. … "I also remember losing to Phoenix the next year, which was heartbreaking. We should have won that Game 7 and didn't. So I have great memories

item.title: How Eugene-Springfield cross-country runners fared at 2026 districts
item.description: The postseason has officially arrived for high school cross-country runners throughout the state of Oregon. item.title: Red Wings interim GM admits Dylan Larkin trade is ‘difficult’ for this reason
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Red Wings interim GM admits Dylan Larkin trade is ‘difficult’ for this reason appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Red Wings have had a difficult season to this point and they find themselves tied for the bottom spot in the Atlantic Division of the Eastern Conference. In addition to trying to find a winning formula, they have had to deal with the trade demand of Dylan Larkin , their former captain. "I got to give Dylan a lot of credit. He went out and played hard for us. Dylan's been here for 12 years. In terms of sitting out, I can't put a timeline on it. With the teams on his list a trade is difficult." pic.twitter.com/NCgPsiZnhY — BucciOT.Com (@Buccigross) October 29, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After making his demand public, Larkin played multiple games for the Red Wings before he let them know that he was not reporting to practice. As a result, the Red Wings have suspended Larkin without pay. “Dylan Larkin has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings,” interim GM Shawn Horcoff said in a statement. “We are disappointed by his decision, particularly given his obligations to the organization and his teammates. We have therefore suspended Dylan without pay.” They are still trying to trade him, but Larkin has a list of just 10 teams that are on his accepted trade list. According to Horcoff, the limited number of teams on Larkin’s trade list makes it more difficult for t he Red Wings to make an acceptable trade . Horcoff has said on multiple occasions that the Red Wings would only make a deal that is beneficial to the team. Horcoff said he appreciated the effort that Larkin demonstrated in the 10 games that he has played this season for Detroit. Larkin had 2 goals and 4 assists in those games. Alex DeBrincat leads the team in scoring with 6 goals and 7 assists in 12 games. Veteran forwards Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson are right behind DeBrincat with 11 and 10 points, respectively. Related: Red Wings officially suspend Dylan Larkin without pay after he bails on team Related: NHL rumors: Red Wings’ Dylan Larkin ‘has had enough,’ won’t play amid trade saga

item.title: DBR Bites #169: Brock Davis Chooses Academics
item.description: Oct 3, 2026; Durham, NC, USA; Duke Blue Devils guard Brock Davis (50) during the Countdown to Craziness at Cameron Indoor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Zachary Taft-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect W e’re back with a new DBR Bites as some news came up on a Thursday that we had to discuss! First, Brock Davis was a late addition to the Duke Men’s Basketball roster in March, helping the team prepare for games during the ACC and NCAA tournaments. He was added to the roster officially for this season. But in the midst of prepping for our Stats Game, Jason discovered that Brock was no longer with the program. We discuss his decision to put his studies before sports and leave the program to focus on his academics. We commend Brock for putting his studies first. We then get into some schedule news for next season, as Duke is slated to play in the Basketball Hall of Fame Series against Arizona in November 2027. That game will take place at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, the home of the Raiders that will be the host of the 2028 Final Four. Once again, Jon Scheyer has accepted all of the smoke and he’s also continuing a couple of trends in playing in Vegas and playing in a city that he hopes the team will return to in April to play for a national title. item.title: Anthony Weaver jokingly calls out reporter for jinxing Ravens’ attempt to stop Josh Allen
item.description: Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Anthony Weaver jokingly calls out reporter for jinxing Ravens’ attempt to stop Josh Allen appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Baltimore Ravens taking on the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, the team’s defense will have a tall task in looking to at least contain superstar quarterback Josh Allen. As it remains to be seen if Lamar Jackson returns from injury for the Ravens against the Bills, the defense will still have to do their part, as defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver speaks about the challenge and even jokes with a reporter about the topic. Talking to the media on Thursday, Weaver was asked about the challenge of stopping Allen, saying that it will “take all of us” to stop him. So far this season in six games, he’s recorded 1,504 passing yards with nine touchdowns and four interceptions, plus 240 yards and eight scores on the ground. “Same as it always is, right? Take takes all 11,” Weaver said, according to Jamison Henley of ESPN. “You got to stop the run, right? First and foremost, try not to give him 50-50 run-pass situations, and we know anytime it is a pass, that can turn into a run too with Josh [Allen]. So, tremendous challenge, tremendous quarterback. We know he’s elite, so it’s going to take all of us.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said “it’s going to take all of us” when it comes to defending Josh Allen . A reporter later pointed out that Baltimore hasn’t allowed a lot of scrambling yards this year, Weaver said: “So, are you’re trying to jinx us now?” pic.twitter.com/P1MOIEK3lx — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) October 29, 2026 After answering that, one member of the media would point out how Baltimore actually has not allowed a lot of rushing yards when a quarterback scrambles, leading to a humorous response from Weaver. “A reporter later pointed out that Baltimore hasn’t allowed a lot of scrambling yards this year, Weaver said: ‘So, you’re trying to jinx us now?'” At any rate, it remains to be seen how Allen will play against the Ravens, as the team looks to snap a two-game skid. Related: Ravens’ Kyle Hamilton eases concerns about knee injury after returning to practice Related: Lamar Jackson will be licking his chops for return after Bills’ Dee Alford injury update

item.title: Christian Watson taken to hospital for chest injury
item.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers receiver Christian Watson was able to walk off the field under his own power when he exited the game on Thursday Night Football against the Carolina Panthers, but it doesn’t look like he’ll return to the game. The Packers officially ruled him out with a chest injury, but the game broadcast said Watson is being taken to a local hospital as a precaution. The broadcast also showed him getting into the ambulance. Video of #Packers WR Christian Watson getting into the ambulance to be taken to the hospital: pic.twitter.com/15ggu6GXak https://t.co/ukOaj2TZvY — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 30, 2026 Watson had been one of Green Bay’s big-play threats this year through the air, helping make up for their lack of a ground game. Because of two other injuries to the slot position (Jayden Reed and Skyy Moore) earlier this season, the Packers are now down to Matthew Golden, Savion Williams, Bo Melton, J. Michael Sturdivant and Coleman Owen at the receiver position for the remainder of the game. Green Bay also only has two tight ends on the field currently, as tight end Josh Whyle has exited the match with a concussion and Jonnu Smith was a healthy scratch on Thursday. We’ll keep you updated on any developments in Watson’s injury status.

item.title: Michael Kay defends Pat McAfee: ‘People don’t know what this business is like’
item.description: Credit: The Michael Kay Show; Kirby Lee - Imagn Images Pat McAfee opened up this week about his fears as a public figure and live performer, sparking a full news cycle of industry responses. The daily show host and College GameDay star took issue with the University of Utah for egging on its students to tease McAfee in a social media video, alluding to the murder of Charlie Kirk at nearby Utah Valley University in a long rant on his show Monday. Later, a report revealed the FBI contacted McAfee about his safety after Kirk’s death, which McAfee confirmed on Thursday . While McAfee seemed to leap to the conclusion that the Utes’ social media video could endanger him while he hosted GameDay , longtime New York City sports host Michael Kay defended the controversial ESPN star on his radio show. “Did he extrapolate too much? Well, we don’t know what he’s feeling,” Kay said Thursday on his ESPN New York show. “We don’t know the fear that he has about taking the stage every day in front of all those kids.” Kay then directed his attention toward McAfee’s critics . “People are saying he’s thin-skinned and that he reads everything about him. You’re all full of it,” he said. “Pat McAfee is grilled every single time he opens his mouth. Maybe he’s not your cup of tea, but I’ll tell you what. He’s built one heck of a career, and he’s making a truckload of money. And he’s on every major portal that ESPN has. Everything. Monday Night Football , College GameDay , and then he has his show, which he owns. Brilliant businessman, and knows exactly about the zeitgeist of this country. But we’re going to tell him that he shouldn’t be thin-skinned. You people don’t know what this business is like.” ICYMI: @RealMichaelKay defends @PatMcAfeeShow. https://t.co/Yl1Vhu9Wpj — ESPN New York (@ESPNNewYork) October 29, 2026 Of course, successful public figures often get the most criticism. As Kay acknowledged about his own hyper-awareness toward what the audience is saying, it is part of the job. But Kay defended McAfee’s engagement with that noise as well. “Don’t tell him that he shouldn’t care about the critics or the people that say nasty things about him,” Kay said. “You get in this position. You see what it feels like. You see if it’s fun. You see if it doesn’t make you second-guess some of the stuff you do. Even though most of the people that are saying it, they would have no idea how to do your job, and couldn’t do it one-hundredth as well as you do.” Some of what the Utes’ video teased McAfee about, and what fans dislike about him, relates to his persona as a sports host. But much of the disdain for McAfee also comes from the guests he books, his commentary on political and social issues, and his frequent embrace of the Trump administration. McAfee noted this in a post on X following his on-air monologue. McAfee complains that outlets take him out of context and don’t cover him fairly on these matters. He often pushes back against media narratives when he feels wronged.

Well, we don’t know what he’s feeling,” Kay said Thursday on his ESPN New York show. “We don’t know the fear that he has about taking the stage every day in front of all those kids.” Kay then directed his attention toward McAfee’s critics . “People are saying he’s thin-skinned and that he reads everything about him. You’re all full of it,” he said. “Pat McAfee is grilled every single time he opens his mouth. Maybe he’s not your cup of tea, but I’ll tell you what. He’s built one heck of a career, and he’s making a truckload of money. And he’s on every major portal that ESPN has. Everything. Monday Night Football , College GameDay , and then he has his show, which he owns. Brilliant businessman, and knows exactly about the zeitgeist of this country. But we’re going to tell him that he shouldn’t be thin-skinned. You people don’t know what this business is like.” ICYMI: @RealMichaelKay defends @PatMcAfeeShow. https://t.co/Yl1Vhu9Wpj — ESPN New York (@ESPNNewYork) October 29, 2026 Of course, successful public figures often get the most criticism. As Kay acknowledged about his own hyper-awareness toward what the audience is saying, it is part of the job. But Kay defended McAfee’s engagement with that noise as well. “Don’t tell him that he shouldn’t care about the critics or the people that say nasty things about him,” Kay said. “You get in this position. You see what it feels like. You see if it’s fun. You see if it doesn’t make you second-guess some of the stuff you do. Even though most of the people that are saying it, they would have no idea how to do your job, and couldn’t do it one-hundredth as well as you do.” Some of what the Utes’ video teased McAfee about, and what fans dislike about him, relates to his persona as a sports host. But much of the disdain for McAfee also comes from the guests he books, his commentary on political and social issues, and his frequent embrace of the Trump administration. McAfee noted this in a post on X following his on-air monologue. McAfee complains that outlets take him out of context and don’t cover him fairly on these matters. He often pushes back against media narratives when he feels wronged. Kay believes it is nearly impossible for someone like McAfee to ignore the chatter about them. If that is the case and the chatter gets under his skin, it may ultimately signal that McAfee is overexposed and should avoid the spotlight when he can. The post Michael Kay defends Pat McAfee: ‘People don’t know what this business is like’ appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Ex-player issues Masyn Winn demand to Cardinals
item.description: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Ex-player issues Masyn Winn demand to Cardinals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . St. Louis Cardinals shortstop Masyn Winn features a high ceiling. Winn earned a Gold Glove in 2025. He displayed offensive potential as well, but in 2026 Winn hit just .232 with a .625 OPS. Former MLB star pitcher Lance Lynn isn’t placing all of the blame on Winn for his offensive struggles, though. Lynn believes the Cardinals need to make a lineup adjustment next season. “If you do not put Masyn Winn in the top of the lineup to do what Masyn Winn is capable of, you keep putting him in a hole,” Lynn said, via Cardinal Territory. “You gotta free him up… Last year, when you put him in the three hole, you just put him in a spot to just not be successful. I don’t know how else to say it. When you put him in the nine hole, it’s kind of disrespectful to his talent.” It’s an intriguing take. The Cardinals could certainly try putting Winn at the top of the lineup and see what happens. Perhaps it could lead to him finding more overall offensive consistency. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Oliver Marmol is expected to remain as manager , so he knows Winn’s skill set well. He’s going to do whatever he thinks is best. Lynn’s take could catch his attention, though. With stars such as Jordan Walker and JJ Wetherholt leading the way, St. Louis’ lineup does feature potential. A breakout offensive season from Winn would give the lineup even more necessary depth. Winn is a tremendous defender, so he could emerge as one of the best all-around shortstops in the game if his offense improves next year.

item.title: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor is the last longstanding veteran pillar remaining, for now
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday, Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, who’s arguably the franchise’s last longstanding veteran cornerstone still remaining after the recent trades of both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, indicated that he has not requested a trade from the only organization he’s ever known. However, he did acknowledge his current uncertain future, which still appears to be very fluid in Indianapolis: #Colts RB Jonathan Taylor confirmed that he has *NOT* requested a trade, but he acknowledged that he doesn’t have full control of his future. — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) October 29, 2026 As a major subject of ongoing trade rumors, Taylor seems proud and comfortable to continue to wear the Horseshoe, and earlier reports indicated that Indianapolis team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon potentially considers Taylor a major part of the Colts recently jumpstarted rebuilding efforts . That being said, Taylor is 27-years-old with 1,691 career carries in the NFL and 926 more collegiately at Wisconsin, at a running back position where players typically don’t age gracefully past the age of 30-years-old. Either the Colts or an acquiring team are realistically looking at 2-3 prime years left regarding Taylor, and for Indianapolis, that’s likely about the minimum amount of time that it would take to complete a successful rebuild these days—assuming conditions go well with a new quarterback, head coach, and general manager all likely. However, keeping a future Colts Ring of Honor player and potential Hall of Famer in the building around young players could be a beneficial thing as far as teaching them an elite work ethic, preparation, approach, etc. It seems to me that the Colts could be persuaded to trade Taylor soon, but it would have to take a significant haul in draft capital from a suitor, presumably the ask right now appears to be at least a first round pick, maybe more. Whether that asking price will go down, like say a second round pick, as we get closer to this year’s trade deadline on Tuesday, November 10th, remains to be seen. However, for now, Taylor is still remaining in Indianapolis.

item.description: Eight straight losses give a team plenty of practice at losing. On Thursday night, Rutgers found a way they had not tried yet. Ryan McAleer followed with three of her own from 6-8 to 6-11, an ace on Kaila Kalama-Bajet in the middle of it and a Rutgers timeout at 6-10 that did not stop it. The set had three ties and one lead change, all of it before 5-6. Karis Willow, off the bench, kept Rutgers attached with five kills in the set, four of them off Baldwin. Tindall did more. She killed six times in the first, three of them in four rallies from 8-14 to 9-16 with the media timeout arriving at 9-15, and Purdue led by six or more the rest of the way. Then Romes ended it herself. She hit out for 14-23, Rutgers called time, and she hit out again for set point. Willow saved one at 15-24, and on the next rally Kate Hansen and Mambu stuffed Romes. Three of Purdue’s last four points were Romes attack errors. Rutgers hit .111 in the set. Purdue hit .355. The second was cleaner and went the same way. Hansen served Purdue to 0-3 with an ace on Kenzie Dyrstad, Jesewitz solo-stuffed Heaney at 2-4, and Romes went to the line and aced MaryKate Scheumann and Tindall on back-to-back serves to tie it 4-4. That was the only tie of the set. Schara answered the same way, acing Alleigh Dutton twice in a row for 4-7. Heaney and Hansen killed on McAleer’s serve for 6-10 and another Rutgers timeout, and Purdue led by three or more for the rest of the set. Rutgers got as close as 15-18 on a Willow kill off a Dutton set. That was as close as it got. Jesewitz hit out on McAleer’s serve, Rutgers burned its second timeout at 15-20, and Mambu and Heaney killed on the next two rallies. Baldwin was called for a handling error at 16-24, George and a Heaney attack error saved two set points, and Mambu ended it 18-25 off an Isabelle Bardin set. Heaney had six kills in the set. Rutgers hit .306, their best set of the night, and lost it by seven because Purdue hit .371 and served four aces, every one of them on a named passer with Kenzie Dyrstad, Dutton twice and Jesewitz. A Wire-to-Wire Third, Then 11 Straight on Sienna Foster’s Serve George opened the third with a kill off a Kenzie Dyrstad set, then aced McAleer and Tindall on consecutive serves for 3-0 before missing her third. Rutgers never trailed and never let it get tied. Purdue missed four serves in the set and committed seven attack errors, and two of the misses, by Schara and McAleer, came in the 7-3 and 9-4 rallies that built the first real lead. Rutgers led 15-8 at the media timeout after Bianka Lulic hit out on Baldwin’s serve, and Heaney hit out on the next one for 16-8. Willow and Romes stuffed Mambu at 18-9 to bring Purdue’s only timeout of the night. Jesewitz and Robinson stuffed Heaney at 22-12, and Baldwin, of all people, put away a Dutton set for 24-13. Eleven set points. Rutgers needed four of them. Dutton served into the net, Bardin aced the next ball and Tindall killed off her, and Bardin finally ended it by missing a serve of her own, 25-16. Rutgers hit .300 with two errors on 30 swings. Purdue hit .065. It was Rutgers’ first set win since Michigan State six days earlier. The fourth started like a match. Hansen solo-stuffed Robinson on the first rally, George killed and aced Tindall for 2-1, and the teams traded through six ties and four lead changes in the first 16 rallies. Rutgers got a point on a Taylor Anderson bad set at 4-5, Jesewitz and Romes stuffed Heaney to tie it 5-5, Romes killed twice for 6-5 and 7-6, and Willow and Romes stuffed Mambu on Kalama-Bajet’s serve for 8-6. That was the last lead Rutgers held. Mambu killed to side out, Willow hit out on Heaney’s serve for 8-8, and Purdue sent Foster to the line. She aced the first ball she served. Mambu killed. Hansen and Mambu stuffed Romes, Hansen and Anderson stuffed George, and Rutgers called time at 8-12. Anderson killed out of the timeout, Hansen stuffed Romes alone, and Mambu killed into the media timeout at 8-15. Foster aced Kenzie Dyrstad, Hansen killed, Romes hit out, and Mambu killed again for 8-19. Eleven serves, 11 Purdue points, with two aces, five kills, three blocks with Hansen in on all of them and one Romes attack error. Zharia Harris-Waddy, on the floor for the only set she played, finally ended it with a kill off Baldwin at 9-19. George hit out, killed, hit out and killed again over the next four rallies, served Rutgers to 13-21 and was stuffed by Heaney and Charles at 13-23. Robinson hit out for match point, Anderson missed a serve to give one back, and Heaney killed off Anderson to end it. Rutgers hit minus-.088 in the fourth with eight kills and 11 attack errors on 34 swings, five of the errors into the block. Purdue hit .308. Stats Breakdown George led everyone in Scarlet with 12 kills, but needed a match-high 40 swings to get them and made eight attack errors for a .100 line. She added three of Rutgers’ six aces, two assists and seven digs for 15 points, tied with Mambu for the match lead, and Purdue did not ace her once. Maxwell, who played the first two sets against Illinois, did not appear, and Howell missed a third straight match. Willow had nine kills on 25 swings with three errors off the bench, .240, and all nine came in the first two sets. She had none in the third and fourth, which is the season’s pattern compressed into one night, very good for a stretch and then gone. Robinson had the steadiest line in Scarlet, eight kills on 19 attempts at .263 with two block assists. Romes finished with seven kills and six errors on 19 swings, .053, plus two aces and four block assists for 11 points. All six of her errors came in two stretches, three in the first set’s last four rallies and three during Foster’s run. Jesewitz hit .074 on 27 swings with five kills and three errors, tied Romes for the team lead with four blocks, one of them solo, and was aced twice. Baldwin set 32 of Rutgers’ 39 assists, added two kills on five swings and led the team with 11 digs. Lily Bolen started all four sets and did not record an assist, so the two-setter split came out 32 to zero. Rutgers served six aces against eight errors, with Dutton missing four, and Purdue out-dug Rutgers 54-49. Mambu, a Georgia Tech transfer, came off the Purdue bench for 13 kills on 29 swings, .310, five of them in the fourth. Hansen hit .667 with six kills and no errors on nine swings and had a match-high six blocks, two solo and four in the fourth. item.title: Why Clemson’s Terrifying Halloween Trip to Florida State Could Haunt Dabo Swinney Forever
item.description: clemson-fsu Heavy Reeling from a 20-16 homecoming setback against Virginia Tech, the Clemson Tigers (4-3, 2-2 ACC) march into Doak S. Campbell Stadium on Saturday to battle the Florida State Seminoles (3-4, 1-3 ACC) on Halloween night. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ACC Network as two of the ACC’s traditional heavyweights collide on the exact 130th anniversary of Clemson’s first game in program history — an 1896 victory over Furman. Together, Clemson and Florida State have accounted for 13 of the past 15 ACC titles and 15 of 17 ACC Championship Game appearances since 2009. How to Watch and Listen: Clemson at Florida State Date: Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 Time: 7 p.m. ET Location: Doak S. Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee, Fla. (Capacity: 67,277) Television: ACC Network Play-by-Play: Wes Durham Analyst: Max Browne Sideline Reporter: Madison Fitzpatrick Radio: Clemson Athletic Network Play-by-Play: Don Munson Color Commentator: Jeff Scott Analyst: Tim Bourret Satellite Radio: SiriusXM Channel 258 Key Storylines 1. Swinney Chasing Bowden, Saban, and Stoops in Tallahassee Two seasons ago at Doak Campbell Stadium, Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney surpassed legendary Florida State coach Bobby Bowden for the most overall victories as an ACC head coach. On Saturday, Swinney (116-30 in ACC regular season play) can tie Bowden’s conference record of 117 ACC regular season victories. A win would also move Swinney (191-56) past Nick Saban (191) and Bob Stoops (191) for sole possession of the second-most wins through the first 20 seasons of an FBS head coaching career, trailing only Tom Osborne (195), despite Swinney coaching only his 19th season and 18th full campaign. The blueprint for that ascent traces back to Swinney’s early days at the helm: “I had a conversation with Terry Don and said, ‘Terry Don, I know we are not very good right now, but we need to play people because that is going to help me teach and help me develop the culture and the mindset that you have to have to win at the highest level,'” recounted Swinney of former athletic director Terry Don Phillips. “I didn’t think we had that, and that’s what we committed to. That’s what we’ve done.” Clemson has taken four straight meetings in Tallahassee and is attempting to become only the third opposing program in college football history to win five consecutive road games against Florida State, joining Florida (1966-76) and Miami (1957-77). The Tigers are also 43-13 following a loss under Swinney and have won 37 consecutive games against opponents with a losing record. 2. Nolan Hauser’s Groza-Caliber Leg and Special Teams Fireworks Under Swinney and special teams coordinator Rich Bisaccia, Clemson features one of the most dangerous special teams units in the nation. The Tigers are one of only two programs nationally with returners ranking inside the FBS Top 15 in both punt return average (Bryant Wesco Jr., 10th at 14.9) and kickoff return average (Chris Johnson Jr., 12th at 24.6). Junior placekicker

Campbell Stadium on Saturday to battle the Florida State Seminoles (3-4, 1-3 ACC) on Halloween night. How to Watch and Listen: Clemson at Florida State Date: Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 Time: 7 p.m. ET Location: Doak S. Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee, Fla. (Capacity: 67,277) Television: ACC Network Play-by-Play: Wes Durham Analyst: Max Browne Sideline Reporter: Madison Fitzpatrick Radio: Clemson Athletic Network Play-by-Play: Don Munson Color Commentator: Jeff Scott Analyst: Tim Bourret Satellite Radio: SiriusXM Channel 258 Key Storylines 1. Swinney Chasing Bowden, Saban, and Stoops in Tallahassee Two seasons ago at Doak Campbell Stadium, Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney surpassed legendary Florida State coach Bobby Bowden for the most overall victories as an ACC head coach. On Saturday, Swinney (116-30 in ACC regular season play) can tie Bowden’s conference record of 117 ACC regular season victories. A win would also move Swinney (191-56) past Nick Saban (191) and Bob Stoops (191) for sole possession of the second-most wins through the first 20 seasons of an FBS head coaching career, trailing only Tom Osborne (195), despite Swinney coaching only his 19th season and 18th full campaign. The blueprint for that ascent traces back to Swinney’s early days at the helm: “I had a conversation with Terry Don and said, ‘Terry Don, I know we are not very good right now, but we need to play people because that is going to help me teach and help me develop the culture and the mindset that you have to have to win at the highest level,'” recounted Swinney of former athletic director Terry Don Phillips. “I didn’t think we had that, and that’s what we committed to. That’s what we’ve done.” Clemson has taken four straight meetings in Tallahassee and is attempting to become only the third opposing program in college football history to win five consecutive road games against Florida State, joining Florida (1966-76) and Miami (1957-77). The Tigers are also 43-13 following a loss under Swinney and have won 37 consecutive games against opponents with a losing record. 2. Nolan Hauser’s Groza-Caliber Leg and Special Teams Fireworks Under Swinney and special teams coordinator Rich Bisaccia, Clemson features one of the most dangerous special teams units in the nation. The Tigers are one of only two programs nationally with returners ranking inside the FBS Top 15 in both punt return average (Bryant Wesco Jr., 10th at 14.9) and kickoff return average (Chris Johnson Jr., 12th at 24.6). Junior placekicker Nolan Hauser is assembling a Lou Groza Award-worthy campaign. Hauser is 18-of-19 on field goals, tying for the national lead in makes (18) and games with three or more field goals (four), while leading all FBS kickers with 702 cumulative yards on made field goals. Hauser, whose 56-yard walk-off winner in the 2024 ACC title game was labeled by Swinney as “the biggest kick in Clemson history,” made history again last week against Virginia Tech. Deployed as a deep punter, Hauser drilled a 63-yard punt down to the Hokies’ 3-yard line, becoming the first FBS player since 2021 to hit three field goals and boot a 60-plus-yard punt in the same contest. Hauser enters Saturday sitting at an 82.8% career field goal mark, within a whisper of Bob Paulling’s school-record 82.9%. 3. Tait Reynolds and Developing Offensive Depth True freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds makes his fifth start behind center, looking to make Clemson 24-17 in starts by first-year signal-callers since 1972. Reynolds is aiming to run for a touchdown in consecutive weeks and lead the team in rushing in back-to-back games, a feat last accomplished by DJ Uiagalelei in 2022. On the outside, wideout T.J. Moore has caught a pass in 34 consecutive contests, needing one reception Saturday to pass Aaron Kelly for the sixth-longest streak in Clemson history. Junior receiver Bryant Wesco Jr. seeks his eighth career 100-yard receiving game to tie Tee Higgins and Perry Tuttle for fifth in school history, while also sitting one punt return touchdown shy of matching the program career record of two. Tyler Brown also aims to become Clemson’s first receiver with eight or more receptions in consecutive games since Amari Rodgers in 2020. The staff continues to lean on spreading snaps across the roster, adhering directly to Swinney’s rotational philosophy: “We’re fully committed to playing guys who deserve to play,” Swinney said. “You commit to a guy early in the season, and even if a guy has only played 10 percent of the snaps, when you get to game eight or nine, they’ve got some good experience.” 4. Heldt, Brown, and the “TANOGA” Defensive Surge Clemson’s defense limited Virginia Tech to a season-low 234 total yards and 1.9 yards per rush, yet the Tigers are hungry to end an eight-game dry spell without winning the turnover battle. That emphasis is drilled every week during “TANOGA Tuesday,” standing for ” Take A ways, NO G iveA ways.” Defensive end Will Heldt enters Tallahassee as one of only two FBS defenders with three multiple-sack games this fall. Heldt has 8.5 tackles for loss and 6.0 sacks in 2026, standing 1.5 tackles for loss away from becoming the 35th FBS player in the College Football Playoff era with three separate seasons of 10.0 TFLs and 5.0 sacks. Behind him, junior linebacker Sammy Brown (eight career double-digit tackle performances) needs one more 10-tackle effort to pass his position coach Ben Boulware and move within one of Kendall Joseph for the most by a Tiger in Swinney’s tenure. In the secondary, cornerback Elliot Washington II aims to build on his team-leading three interceptions. 5. Halloween Hex and Finishing in the Fourth Quarter Clemson holds a 15-7 all-time mark on Halloween (9-5 away from home) and aims to hold an 11th consecutive ACC road opponent to 24 or fewer points. Analytics continue to highlight the “Middle Eight” — the four minutes before and after halftime — as one of the critical “games within the game” where Clemson has posted an 80-5 record since 2015 when outscoring foes. While the program cherishes its traditions born “Where the Blue Ridge yawns its greatness, where the Tigers play…”, the focus heading into Tallahassee remains winning the final 15 minutes. That charge is captured on Death Valley’s screens before every final frame through retired strength coach Joey Batson’s words in the “This is Why We Work” video: “Let me tell you something right now: they don’t put championship rings on smooth hands! You gotta go earn it! You gotta go earn it six seconds at a time! You win championships when the stadium is empty, when the band ain’t playing, when the cheerleaders ain’t cheering, when it’s just you and your brothers right beside you. That’s when you win championships! In the fourth quarter, that is when we shine!” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Why Clemson’s Terrifying Halloween Trip to Florida State Could Haunt Dabo Swinney Forever appeared first on HEAVY .

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) Getty Los Angeles Clippers, and possible future Lakers forward Derrick Jones Jr. Getty While the Los Angeles Lakers may have briefly filled one hole in the roster with a new backup center by waiving AK Okereke to sign Lawson Lovering, there are still a few potential moves the team can make to upgrade at the forward position. One name in particular mentioned in trade rumors has been Derrick Jones Jr. of the Los Angeles Clippers, and after his strong showing against the Lakers on Wednesday night, he continues to look like a top trade target for the front office to land a new starting wing on the roster. Jones finished the game with 15 points, five rebounds, four steals, and two blocks in 28 minutes, and after that solid performance, the idea of him making his way to the Lakers only becomes more intriguing after what he showed on the court going up against the team. Lakers Urged To Make Derrick Jones Trade Getty INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA – APRIL 09: Derrick Jones Jr. #55 of the LA Clippers during play against the Houston Rockets in the second half at Intuit Dome on April 09, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) After his latest outing against the Lakers, which came only days after the two sides matched up last week, Svyatoslav Rovenchuk urged the franchise to once again look at Jones as a trade target option. “The Los Angeles Lakers got two close-up looks at Derrick Jones Jr. in their head-to-heads against the crosstown Los Angeles Clippers. DJJ followed up an impressive first go-around with another head-turning performance,” he wrote. “The first time the Clippers and Lakers played, Jones was the primary defender who helped force his old teammate, Luka Doncic , to commit a career-high 11 turnovers…(On Wednesday) the athletic forward was as disruptive as his team could have asked for. He once again was the lead cause of a high turnover night for the Lakers star he was guarding. Reaves finished the game with 8 giveaways.” Jones is averaging 12.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.8 assists, and 1.8 steals on 57.6% shooting in four games so far this season, the best averages of his 11-year career so far. While he showed a ton of promise on the defensive end of the floor against the Lakers, he’s a decent offensive option, and as a trade target, he could arrive as a plug-and-play forward who would immediately upgrade the roster. Derrick Jones Jr. is a sick player archetype, vertical spacing 3&D wing…Insane dunker/oop catcher. Solid spot up shooter. Versatile defender that can hang with apex ball-handling wings while also providing weakside rim protection. Winning player. pic.twitter.com/nueXbdD03S — Basketball University (@UofBasketball) August 29, 2026 The Lakers saw a strong game from Matisse Thybulle, and also have Ziaire Williams , Jake LaRavia , and a few other reserves to play on the wings right now. However, Jones might be a slight upgrade from all of them. “Even so, if February comes around, and Rob Pelinka wants to make an all-in push before the deadline, one would imagine Jones near the top of the targets list,” Rovenchuk added about the team’s forward depth. “There were murmurings in the offseason about the Clippers’ willingness to operate in good faith so Jones can get to his next team, should that be something he wants before his contract expires at season’s end. If DJJ points across town, one would imagine the Lakers will have plenty of interest.” As time goes on, the Lakers will have a better understanding of the options they have on the wings. But if the front office and coaching staff aren’t happy with some of the names mentioned above, Jones could be the missing piece to raise the ceiling of this team around its star trio. Los Angeles Remains Linked To The Top 3-And-D Wing Target Getty The Los Angeles Lakers remain linked in trade rumors to Derrick Jones Jr. as a top forward target. While just on paper Jones would be a solid fit to join the Lakers starting lineup, Rovenchuk’s comments aren’t the first time he’s been mentioned as a top trade target for the Purple and Gold. Previously, it was Maxwell Odgen, who named the 29-year-old a ‘dream outcome’ and ‘ultimate’ wing for the Lakers to go after in a deal. “The dream outcome here would be for Derrick Jones Jr. to end up with the Lakers. Jones is an elite wing defender who excels at the point of attack, as well as a capable three-point shooter who played alongside Doncic when the Mavericks made their run to the NBA Finals,” he wrote. “Compounded by his experience alongside Doncic, Jones is the ultimate trade target. It could prove costly to bring him on, but with an expiring contract and an ideal skill set for Los Angeles’ system, it’s at least worth exploring.” More recently, answering questions on a Reddit AMA , Lakers reporter Dan Woike of The Athletic brought Jones’ name back up as a realistic Lakers trade target, as the Clippers could make him available in a deal. “I’ve heard the Clippers really value Derrick Jones Jr. as a player and behind the scenes, but if he were available, the Lakers would probably call and hope it turned out better than their last deal with LAC,” Woike said. On fit alone, and given his experience playing with Doncic, Jones is exactly the type of player the Lakers wanted this summer but failed to land. He wouldn’t need the ball in his hands much, but he’s above average on both ends, while offering spacing and some rim-running ability to get easy looks from Doncic, Reaves, and Collin Sexton in the two-man game. Playing Jones alongside Walker Kessler would boost the Lakers’ defense, which they could use, and though it’s uncertain what the Clippers would want back in a trade, if using Jarred Vanderbilt ‘s contract, along with Jaden Hardy or a second-round pick, can get a deal done, that might be worth it for general manager Rob Pelinka to pick up the phone. The Lakers already filled the backup center hole with a low-risk move, but if the team is ready to take a bigger gamble, Jones might be the best trade target available in the final year of his current contract. item.title: The school of champions: Park Hill sees 2 alums win World Series, NBA title 4 months apart
item.description: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — The school of champions? That certainly has a nice ring to it for one Kansas City metro school. Park Hill High School saw two of their former athletes win championships in a major professional sport in the same calendar year. It started with Landry Shamet, who made huge contributions off the bench en route to the New York Knicks winning the 2026 NBA Finals. Shamet shot 91.7% from three, the highest ever three-point percentage for a single playoff series with at least 10 attempts. HyVee Team of the Week: Blue Valley West volleyball Then, just four months later, Milwaukee Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby hoisted a World Series championship trophy after putting on a record-setting postseason performance. Ashby set the record for the most consecutive scoreless playoff innings in MLB history. What makes the moment even better. The two have a well-documented friendship that started at a sport neither plays: A Park Hill High School football game. The two have shown vast amounts of support each other. Ashby was seen wearing Shamet's jersey back in June, while the Knicks were in the finals, and Shamet rocked Ashby's jersey before Game 1 of the World Series last week. Mizzou RB Ahmad Hardy to play in first game since being shot "We grew up together going to high school and basically became best friends. He's just an amazing human being," Ashby said back in June. One comes out the bullpen. One comes off the bench. Both are breaking records. And now, both are champions. Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved. item.title: Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
item.description: 1 Min Read Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 PIA26802 Credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech/USGS Photojournal Navigation Science Photojournal Map Showing Potential Origins… Photojournal Home Photojournal Search Latest Content Galleries Feedback RSS About Downloads Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 JPEG (1.22 MB) Description This global map of Mars shows 13 locations that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth. While scientists can never know for sure where a Martian meteorite originated, Teghaza 001 includes clues that link it to highlands in the southern hemisphere of the Red Planet. The base map of this image was produced with data from the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter instrument aboard NASA’s Mars Global Surveyor mission. Scientists used data from NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter to identify areas of the map (noted with white circles) that have similar mineralogy and chemistry as Teghaza 001. item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Bruno Fernandes owes Manchester United a performance, Mathys Tel has arrived at Spurs and Liverpool are improving Premier League top scorers Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes held clear-the-air talks this week. Fernandes was an unused substitute against Bournemouth after criticising Carrick’s tactics during the Champions League defeat by Como but it seems the situation has been resolved – for now. Dropping Fernandes did not do United any good against Bournemouth, who ran riot at Old Trafford , and the captain is expected to return to the starting lineup for the trip to Chelsea. If that happens, he owes Carrick a performance. Fernandes has been poor this season and it is time he did his talking on the pitch.
