item.title: Patrick Stewart, renowned actor and ‘Star Trek’s’ Captain Picard, dies at 86
item.description: null Less than a week after the fates took Walter Koenig from our galaxy, another " Star Trek " legend has left us: Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. According to his spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak, the beloved Shakespearean actor passed away on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at his Los Angeles home after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Bush Novak shared. "We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace." Patrick Stewart in director John Boorman's spectacular film, "Excalibur." (Image credit: Warner Bros.) The first time I ever saw Patrick Stewart was in director John Boorman’s masterful 1981 King Arthur film, "Excalibur." As a young teenager, I was immediately captivated by his commanding presence and charisma portraying King Leodegrance of Cameliard — Queen Guinevere’s noble father and a cunning warrior. In 1984, he entered the sci-fi realm in David Lynch's grand and ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert's "Dune," in which he played Paul Atreides' good friend and mentor, War Master Gurney Halleck. Patrick Stewart in David Lynch's "Dune" from 1984. (Image credit: Universal Pictures) Stewart was later cast as the U.S.S. Enterprise’s Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation . He entranced millions of viewers in this role, traveling the final frontier with his gallant crew and redefining the brave and compassionate traits of a Federation starship commander. His adventurous journey on that popular show, a spinoff of "Star Trek: The Original Series," ran from 1987 to 1994, encompassing 178 episodes across seven seasons confronting Klingons, Cardassians, Romulans and The Borg. When the series ended, Stewart continued on in the Enterprise's center seat by starring in four "Star Trek" feature films: 1994’s "Star Trek: Generations," 1996’s "Star Trek: First Contact," 1998’s "Star Trek: Insurrection," and 2002’s "Star Trek: Nemesis." Stewart also reprised the role of Jean-Luc Picard in three seasons of Paramount+’s " Star Trek: Picard ," which ran from 2020 to 2023. Stewart's prodigious talent was on further display in the hit adaptations of Marvel’s " The X-Men ." He played the powerful, wheelchair-bound telepath Professor Charles Xavier in 2000’s "X-Men," 2003’s "X2: X-Men United," 2006’s "X-Men: The Last Stand," 2014’s "X-Men: Days of Future Past," and 2017’s "Logan." Stewart, and Xavier, were prominently featured in those films. The actor and character also appeared in 2009’s "X-Men Origins: Wolverine" and 2013’s "The Wolverine," and will do so again in " Avengers: Doomsday ," which will be released around Christmastime this year. Aside from the two "Star Trek" and "The X-Men" franchise roles, Stewart had a flourishing career

item.content:encoded: null Less than a week after the fates took Walter Koenig from our galaxy, another " Star Trek " legend has left us: Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. According to his spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak, the beloved Shakespearean actor passed away on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at his Los Angeles home after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Bush Novak shared. "We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace." Patrick Stewart in director John Boorman's spectacular film, "Excalibur." (Image credit: Warner Bros.) The first time I ever saw Patrick Stewart was in director John Boorman’s masterful 1981 King Arthur film, "Excalibur." As a young teenager, I was immediately captivated by his commanding presence and charisma portraying King Leodegrance of Cameliard — Queen Guinevere’s noble father and a cunning warrior. In 1984, he entered the sci-fi realm in David Lynch's grand and ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert's "Dune," in which he played Paul Atreides' good friend and mentor, War Master Gurney Halleck. Patrick Stewart in David Lynch's "Dune" from 1984. (Image credit: Universal Pictures) Stewart was later cast as the U.S.S. Enterprise’s Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation . He entranced millions of viewers in this role, traveling the final frontier with his gallant crew and redefining the brave and compassionate traits of a Federation starship commander. His adventurous journey on that popular show, a spinoff of "Star Trek: The Original Series," ran from 1987 to 1994, encompassing 178 episodes across seven seasons confronting Klingons, Cardassians, Romulans and The Borg. When the series ended, Stewart continued on in the Enterprise's center seat by starring in four "Star Trek" feature films: 1994’s "Star Trek: Generations," 1996’s "Star Trek: First Contact," 1998’s "Star Trek: Insurrection," and 2002’s "Star Trek: Nemesis." Stewart also reprised the role of Jean-Luc Picard in three seasons of Paramount+’s " Star Trek: Picard ," which ran from 2020 to 2023. Stewart's prodigious talent was on further display in the hit adaptations of Marvel’s " The X-Men ." He played the powerful, wheelchair-bound telepath Professor Charles Xavier in 2000’s "X-Men," 2003’s "X2: X-Men United," 2006’s "X-Men: The Last Stand," 2014’s "X-Men: Days of Future Past," and 2017’s "Logan." Stewart, and Xavier, were prominently featured in those films. The actor and character also appeared in 2009’s "X-Men Origins: Wolverine" and 2013’s "The Wolverine," and will do so again in " Avengers: Doomsday ," which will be released around Christmastime this year. Aside from the two "Star Trek" and "The X-Men" franchise roles, Stewart had a flourishing career that spanned radio, stage and screen and was always a stellar attraction at any comic-con or other fan event around the world. Another of his many memorable projects was the compelling one-man stage show in which he played all the characters in Charles Dickens' novella "A Christmas Carol," captured on a two-disc CD set that I listen to each holiday season. Patrick Stewart played the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the popular "X-Men" movies. (Image credit: 20th Century Studios) Knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010, Sir Patrick Stewart leaves behind a remarkable legacy that brought a rare gravitas and humanity to every performance he was ever involved in, and his passing leaves fans, friends and loved ones with heavy hearts. Here’s to a wonderful life well-lived!

item.title: Intel says it’s selling every affordable laptop chip it can make
item.description: During Intel's latest earnings call , CEO Lip-Bu Tan said that demand for its budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips "is outstripping supply." According to CFO David Zinsner, the chips are now sold out. Zinsner said Intel has "seen significant growth in Wildcat Lake. It's coming exactly at the right time because it's cost-optimized and we're seeing a lot of focus in that regard." As shortages of RAM and other components have driven up PC prices over recent months, Intel's Wildcat Lake chips have been appearing in new lower-cost Windows laptops on par with the MacBook Neo, like the new Dell XPS 13 or the HP Omnibook 5 14 . item.title: Slice of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
item.description: 1 Min Read Slice of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 PIA26801 Credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech Photojournal Navigation Science Photojournal Slice of Martian Meteorite… Photojournal Home Photojournal Search Latest Content Galleries Feedback RSS About Downloads Slice of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 JPEG (2.50 MB) PIA26801 Figure A TIFF (26.10 MB) Description This slice of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth, was used to determine the age of the rock. Reflected light images like these serve as a scientist’s road map, helping them find minerals of interest to analyze by different instruments. Figure A Figure A is the same image with annotations showing minerals like iron-titanium oxides (brighter grains) and pyroxene (medium gray), both of which tell a story about the formation of Mars’ crust and mantle. Shocked plagioclase (darker gray) is created by extreme pressures during impacts, including the one that sent Teghaza 001 flying through space to Earth. The alteration represents fine grain carbonate, sulfate and clay minerals formed on Earth. item.title: Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA —PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, especially from opposition leaders, over new loans the country has accessed from international institutions and banks. ‎ ‎In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” to be published on Nigerian news platforms, President Tinubu wrote: “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind.” ‎ ‎He identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and the modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. ‎ ‎The President said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce logistics costs, unlock agricultural and industrial potential and attract private investment. ‎ ‎The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to cut logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent. It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity. ‎ ‎The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services. ‎ ‎According to him: “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.” ‎ ‎He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade. ‎ ‎“We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎He wrote that improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure. ‎ ‎The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets. ‎ ‎He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030. ‎ ‎In an article titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. ‎ ‎He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 b
item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA —PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, especially from opposition leaders, over new loans the country has accessed from international institutions and banks. ‎ ‎In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” to be published on Nigerian news platforms, President Tinubu wrote: “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind.” ‎ ‎He identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and the modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. ‎ ‎The President said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce logistics costs, unlock agricultural and industrial potential and attract private investment. ‎ ‎The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to cut logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent. It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity. ‎ ‎The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services. ‎ ‎According to him: “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.” ‎ ‎He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade. ‎ ‎“We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎He wrote that improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure. ‎ ‎The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets. ‎ ‎He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030. ‎ ‎In an article titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. ‎ ‎He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 billion in net reserves, while the tax-to-GDP ratio increased to 12.5 per cent from seven per cent. ‎ ‎Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. ‎ ‎The President attributed the improvements to measures including petrol subsidy removal, exchange rate unification, tax reforms and coordinated efforts to tackle inflation. ‎ ‎“The decisions taken since 2023 were difficult but necessary,” he said, referring to the reforms. ‎ ‎Tinubu said the gains have strengthened Nigeria’s ability to attract investment and finance projects that support long-term economic growth. ‎ ‎“Confidence has a price; our cost of borrowing is going down, and the country risk premium has drastically decreased,” he said. ‎ ‎The President cited positive assessments by international credit rating agencies as evidence of improved confidence in the economy. ‎ ‎ ‎“These are not political endorsements; they are independent assessments by global rating agencies, index providers, regulators and investors, recognising stronger external reserves, improved macroeconomic management and greater financial credibility,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎According to the President, the improved standing could help Nigeria attract more institutional investors, secure longer-term financing and reduce borrowing costs. ‎ ‎He said the administration was shifting public borrowing away from financing short-term fiscal pressures towards investments that would generate economic returns, create jobs and expand opportunities for future generations. ‎ ‎The President said the government was also pursuing longer-term financing arrangements to match the lifespan of infrastructure assets, reduce refinancing pressures and secure more competitive funding for productive investments. ‎ ‎President Tinubu said Nigeria must convert renewed international confidence into capital expenditure, completed infrastructure and lasting economic benefits for citizens. ‎ ‎He identified five priorities for the next phase of the Federal Executive Council’s economic strategy: food affordability and energy price stability; budget harmonisation and fiscal discipline; completion of high-impact projects and investment in critical infrastructure; an improved economic policy framework and regulatory efficiency; and targeted household support alongside investment in human development. ‎ ‎The President stressed that the success of the current administration’s economic schemes would be measured by completed projects, increased investment, employment generation and improved living standards. ‎ ‎“Securing financing is not the achievement. Completing the project, delivering value and improving the lives of Nigerians is the achievement,” he said. ‎ ‎He added that the nation’s economic ambition must be supported by responsible borrowing and investments that create lasting opportunities for future generations. The post Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Researchers find bugs in 5 AI developer tools, with OpenAI and Microsoft flaws still unpatched
item.description: Multiple vulnerabilities in five popular AI developer tools could allow attackers to execute code on a host machine, read and steal files, or spoof browser address bars. Researchers say flaws in OpenAI's Codex and Microsoft's VS Code remain unpatched, potentially putting developers who use affected configurations at risk. AI security startup Forever Security discovered vulnerabilities in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Anthropic's Claude Desktop, VS Code, and Codex, and disclosed four of the flaws to the affected vendors. GitHub independently fixed the Copilot vulnerability without receiving a report from Forever Security. All five share a common security weakness: embedded browsers granted capabilities beyond those available to conventional browsers. Each tool “enriched its embedded browser beyond what a normal browser allows, and those enrichments undermined the traditional threat model - as agent input, as the authority on a tab’s own address, or as reach onto the host,” Forever researcher Gal Weizman wrote in a Thursday report . Forever dubbed this class of vulnerability “Embrace,” short for EMbedded BRowser, and said the flaws led to code execution in Cursor, data theft in Claude Desktop, Codex, and VS Code, and address bar spoofing in GitHub Copilot. Here’s what each of these looks like, starting with Cursor. Cursor: arbitrary code execution Typical web pages can’t run commands on the host computer because a web page’s JavaScript cannot talk to local apps. Cursor’s integrated browser, however, allows a page to call the agent’s composer. The agent reads this as instructions and follows them, but the instructions remain hidden from human users. This opens the coding agent up to prompt injection attacks that could allow an attacker to execute commands on the host machine. The researchers disclosed the vulnerability to Cursor on September 10, and the vendor silently patched the flaw on October 1. According to Forever, Cursor did not publish a security advisory about the issue or respond to the researchers' disclosure. Cursor also did not reply to The Register ’s request for comment. GitHub Copilot: address bar spoofing Under normal browser operations, a webpage cannot change the content of the address bar. “Copilot’s browser preview works differently,” Weizman wrote. “Some pages change their address without loading a new page, and the app cannot always see that. So Copilot let the page tell the app its own address.” The app checked only whether the text looked like a web address, starting with http, https or file, but it didn’t check where the tab really pointed to. This can be abused to trick the embedded browser into displaying a spoofed URL - such as github.com/login - in the address bar, while loading a fraudulent website - like a phishing page - underneath. The researchers found the address-bar spoofing flaw in GitHub Copilot 1.1.27 on September 26. GitHub independently fixed the flaw in a later Copilot build (1.1.29) on October 13 without receivi

All five share a common security weakness: embedded browsers granted capabilities beyond those available to conventional browsers. Each tool “enriched its embedded browser beyond what a normal browser allows, and those enrichments undermined the traditional threat model - as agent input, as the authority on a tab’s own address, or as reach onto the host,” Forever researcher Gal Weizman wrote in a Thursday report . Forever dubbed this class of vulnerability “Embrace,” short for EMbedded BRowser, and said the flaws led to code execution in Cursor, data theft in Claude Desktop, Codex, and VS Code, and address bar spoofing in GitHub Copilot. Here’s what each of these looks like, starting with Cursor. Cursor: arbitrary code execution Typical web pages can’t run commands on the host computer because a web page’s JavaScript cannot talk to local apps. Cursor’s integrated browser, however, allows a page to call the agent’s composer. The agent reads this as instructions and follows them, but the instructions remain hidden from human users. This opens the coding agent up to prompt injection attacks that could allow an attacker to execute commands on the host machine. The researchers disclosed the vulnerability to Cursor on September 10, and the vendor silently patched the flaw on October 1. According to Forever, Cursor did not publish a security advisory about the issue or respond to the researchers' disclosure. Cursor also did not reply to The Register ’s request for comment. GitHub Copilot: address bar spoofing Under normal browser operations, a webpage cannot change the content of the address bar. “Copilot’s browser preview works differently,” Weizman wrote. “Some pages change their address without loading a new page, and the app cannot always see that. So Copilot let the page tell the app its own address.” The app checked only whether the text looked like a web address, starting with http, https or file, but it didn’t check where the tab really pointed to. This can be abused to trick the embedded browser into displaying a spoofed URL - such as github.com/login - in the address bar, while loading a fraudulent website - like a phishing page - underneath. The researchers found the address-bar spoofing flaw in GitHub Copilot 1.1.27 on September 26. GitHub independently fixed the flaw in a later Copilot build (1.1.29) on October 13 without receiving a vulnerability report from Forever. We reached out to GitHub and did not receive a response. Claude Desktop, Codex, and VS Code: arbitrary file read All three of these vendors’ coding assistants allow local HTML files opened in the built-in browser to escape its boundaries and access other files. Both Claude Desktop and VS Code allow local pages access to their respective project folders, but the researchers found that these restrictions did not apply to web workers – a browser feature that allows JavaScript to run in a background thread, separate from the page's main thread. This means a local page can start a worker, and the worker can bypass restrictions to reach any file on the machine. Codex, however, didn’t have this same restriction, meaning a local page could read any file directly without a worker. Weizman said his team disclosed the issue to Anthropic on July 23, and the AI vendor declined the Claude Desktop bug report as invalid for a “workspace trust” gated security boundary. A day later, however, Noma Security reported the same flaw, according to Weizman, and Anthropic accepted the report as valid. Anthropic did not respond to The Register ’s questions about either bug report or Forever’s timeline of events. Forever disclosed the Codex bug to OpenAI on July 27 and didn’t get a response. The security team says it’s still unpatched. OpenAI did not respond to our inquiries, including if it planned to fix the flaw. On September 10, Forever disclosed the VS Code vulnerability to Microsoft and says the vendor also labeled it as an invalid workspace trust gated security boundary issue. The researchers claim it remains unpatched. Microsoft did not respond to our request for comment.®

item.title: Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend
item.description: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and his girlfriend, Stefanie Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a baby girl named Liora Audrey. Galatasaray, the Turkish club where Osimhen plays, announced the arrival of the couple’s daughter in a social media post on Thursday. “Our Football A Team player Victor Osimhen and Stefanie have welcomed a baby girl into the world. “We congratulate the couple Victor and Stefanie; we wish their newborn baby Liora Audrey a long, healthy, and happy life!” the post read. The couple’s first daughter, Hailey, was born in October 2022. Ladewig, a Cameroonian-German fashion model and social media influencer, reportedly began dating Osimhen in 2019 when the Nigerian forward was playing for German Bundesliga side Wolfsburg. Earlier this month, reports emerged that Ladewig had been involved in a road accident while heavily pregnant. Turkish media reported that she escaped unhurt in the crash, which involved three vehicles. Meanwhile, Osimhen is expected to feature for Galatasaray in their league fixture against T. Konyaspor on Friday, having been included in the squad for the match. The 27-year-old forward was in impressive form on Monday, scoring twice to help Galatasaray defeat their fierce Istanbul rivals, Fenerbahce, in the city derby. Galatasaray currently lead the league standings after nine matches, while Osimhen has scored eight goals, placing him among the competition’s joint-top scorers. The post Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reddit’s CEO says Google’s AI Mode ‘does not drive traffic’
item.description: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said in an earnings call today that Google's AI-powered search modes do not help with traffic to the platform, echoing problems facing other websites and publishers . As part of its Q3 2026 earnings, Reddit revealed that search traffic in October has "dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week," and he attributes part of the company's struggles with Google traffic to how AI Mode and AI Overviews change the search experience. "The reality is, AI Mode does not drive traffic," Huffman says. "Not for us, and not to anybody, as far as I know. That's just a fundamental shift in how Google works. item.title: Everton ease past Newcastle to set up Fleetwood trip after Grealish is dropped
item.description: The biggest night in Everton’s season started with a big call from David Moyes and demanded a big performance from his players. With the exception of Jack Grealish , they did not let him down. A quarter-final at Fleetwood Town is their prize after a clinical, committed display shattered Newcastle’s hopes of lifting the Carabao Cup for a second time in three seasons. Newcastle dominated spells of the fourth round tie and the stats – registering 28 shots to Everton’s 11, although only nine visiting attempts were on target – but individual defensive errors and an ineffective attack proved a ruinous combination. Matthias Jaissle denied his team are a soft touch, despite persuasive evidence to the contrary, yet called Newcastle “naive” and the defeat, in front of almost 8,000 of their fans, “shocking”. Andy Burnham was among the many Evertonians in attendance grateful for Newcastle’s generosity. Continue reading...

item.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.” Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law. “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined. “In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register. “The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said. Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases. The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State. “He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu. On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.” For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed. The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.” “Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said. The post Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28 appeared fi

item.title: PSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopes
item.description: You cannot miss half a dozen big chances at Women’s Champions League level and expect to get away with it. That is the harsh lesson Manchester City learnt on Thursday against Paris Saint-Germain, who extended the English champions’ wait for their first win in Europe this season by striking late to secure a point at a disappointed Joie Stadium. City’s third draw from three Champions League games so far this season really ought to have been a victory. Instead, their hopes of a top-four spot and with it automatic qualification for the quarter-finals are looking increasingly slim. Continue reading...

item.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach League Cup quarter-finals
item.description: Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood. David Moyes’s side took the lead through James Garner’s first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough. Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn’s reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run. Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14. The ‘Cod Army’ caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury. Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984. Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes’s men made light work of their last-16 tie. Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday. Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection “due to a breach of club discipline”. Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training. But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates. – Everton hit their stride – Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later. Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute. Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January. Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time. At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek. Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval. Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford. It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season. Burn scored with a header from Willock’s 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players. But Newcastle’s brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Evert

But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates. – Everton hit their stride – Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later. Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute. Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January. Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time. At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek. Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval. Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford. It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season. Burn scored with a header from Willock’s 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players. But Newcastle’s brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Everton moved a step closer to Wembley. AFP The post Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach League Cup quarter-finals appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Utomi, Ohaa, Yesufu urge Nigerians to mobilise support for Obi
item.description: Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027. The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters. Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges. He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity. According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change. “We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said. Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means. In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance. He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones. According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development. “My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said. Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians. He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections. Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process. item.title: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war in Ukraine
item.description: In tonight's edition, concern is growing in Tunisia as the families of several men who travelled to Russia for work or study are still searching for an answer about the fate of their loved ones forcibly conscripted to the war in Ukraine. Also, a year after Tanzania's controversial election, the fear hasn't faded. And Dakar is ready to make history, as the first Olympic event ever held on African soil gets underway this weekend.

item.title: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
item.description: In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience," adding: Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world. Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users. Read full article Comments

item.title: Inter and Milan unveil plans for new shared stadium to replace San Siro
item.description: Generali Stadium will have 71,500-seat capacity Inter fans protest the plans outside gala event Internazionale and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the shared San Siro venue from the 2031-32 season. The stadium, sponsored by Generali – Italy’s largest insurance company – will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost the two clubs €1.2 billion (£1bn). The plans were revealed at a gala event at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco on Thursday – but some fans in attendance voiced their opposition to San Siro being demolished. Continue reading...

item.title: Halloween Aboard the International Space Station
item.description: ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano finally gets his wish to fly like Superman aboard the International Space Station during Expedition 37. Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit. Whether individually or as an entire crew, they dress up in sometimes spooky, sometimes scary, but always creative costumes, often designed from materials available aboard the space station. Take a look at how the station crews have celebrated in years past. For Halloween 2009, the Expedition 21 crew shows off its costumes. Expedition 21 NASA astronaut Nicole Stott shows off her Halloween costume. In 2017, Expedition 53 crew members show off their Halloween costumes. Flight Engineer Sergei Prokopyev of Roscosmos, dressed as Elvis Presley, Commander Alexander Gerst of ESA as Darth Vader, and Flight Engineer Serena Auñón-Chancellor of NASA as a mad scientist, pose for a Halloween photo inside the Kibo Japanese Experiment Module pressurized module aboard the space station during Expedition 57. Members of Expedition 61, NASA astronaut Christina Koch, top left, ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano, and NASA astronauts Andrew “Drew” Morgan, and Jessica Meir, show off their Halloween spirit in 2019. Expedition 66 crewmembers NASA astronaut Shane Kimbrough, left, Thomas Pesquet of ESA, Akihiko Hoshide of JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), and NASA astronaut Mark Vande Hei show off their Halloween cards. In 2022, Expedition 68 astronauts Koichi Wakata of JAXA, left, and NASA astronauts Francisco “Frank” Rubio, Nicole Mann, and Josh Cassada dressed as popular video game and cartoon characters, using stowage containers in their Halloween costumes and holding improvised trick-or-treat bags. Expedition 70 astronauts Jasmin Moghbeli of NASA, left, Satoshi Furukawa of JAXA, NASA astronaut Loral O’Hara, and ESA astronaut Andreas Mogensen celebrate Halloween 2023. A trio of Expedition 73 astronauts dressed for Halloween in 2025. Follow the astronauts aboard the space station to see how they celebrate holidays in space. The space station remains a vital scientific platform, providing the foundation needed to survive and thrive as humanity ventures into the unexplored territories of our universe. Explore stories, images, and research from more than 25 years of continuous human presence aboard the space station. https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/iss25 Explore More 6 min read NASA Provides Progress Update on Moon Base Rovers Article 1 week ago 3 min read I Am Artemis: Allison Mjoen Article 2 weeks ago 2 min read Power Up: Roll Out Solar Arrays Boost Space Station Power Supply Article 2 weeks ago

item.title: Across Africa: Real estate scams growing in Ivory Coast
item.description: This week in Across Africa: in Ivory Coast, severe housing shortage has fueled demand for land, creating opportunities for fraudsters selling fake properties and non-existent plots. Also, Kenya’s women are changing the game. From the track to the boxing ring, female athletes are delivering some of the country’s biggest sporting successes. And Addis Ababa pushes ahead with ambitious plans to become East Africa’s clean-energy powerhouse.

item.title: I’ll work closely with Kwankwaso if elected, Obi reassures
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has reiterated willingness to work closely with his vice-presidential candidate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to move the country forward. Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during a town hall meeting in Enugu, where he engaged supporters and stakeholders on the country’s challenges and his vision for national development. The former Anambra State governor said they would work together to tackle insecurity and restore safety across Nigeria if elected president in 2027. He said that securing lives and property would be a priority of his administration, promising to confront the security challenges threatening communities and livelihoods across the country. The presidential candidate regretted that the current administration had failed to protect the lives and property of Nigerians, which he maintained was the primary responsibility. Obi assured voters in the South East to vote for him because of his competence and ability to tackle challenges facing the nation. He challenged other presidential candidates to meet and discuss their plans, and warned the people not to be deceived by rhetoric and propaganda. On education, Obi said he would declare a state of emergency on education to enable his administration to tackle the issue of out-of-school children head-on, hinting that Nigerian children deserved quality education. In his remarks, the vice-presidential candidate of NDC, Kwankwaso, advised that nobody should be deceived by ethnicity, saying, “It’s obvious that Nigerians are going through numerous difficulties”. Kwankwaso lamented that people were facing challenges like insecurity, unemployment, poverty, hunger and so many other challenges. He explained that the only solution to achieve a new Nigeria was unity, diligence, perseverance and willingness. He urged Nigerians to come out en masse to cast, protect and follow up on their votes until results were announced, noting that it was not a one-man show but a collective responsibility. Also, Sen Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly, described Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso, as the “best presidential ticket” to lead Nigeria. Umeh expressed confidence that the South-East would rally behind Obi in the 2027 presidential election, urging the people to remain resolute and resist attempts to intimidate or discourage them from pursuing their political choice. He also commended the resilience of supporters who, according to him, ensured that the meeting held despite reported attempts to frustrate the gathering. The senator further praised Kwankwaso for his efforts to build support in Northern Nigeria, expressing optimism that the Obi-led ticket could attract votes across the country. Umeh urged the people of the South-East to use their votes to make a strong political statement in 2027, declaring his support for Obi’s presidential ambition and calling on the region to unite behind the project. (NAN) Th

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 29, 1991: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by asteroid Gaspra and snaps amazing photos while flying at 18,000 mph
item.description: null On Oct. 29, 1991, the Galileo spacecraft flew by the asteroid Gaspra on its way to Jupiter. Gaspra was the first asteroid to ever be visited by a spacecraft. Gaspra orbits near the inner edge of the asteroid belt . The Galileo spacecraft had been travelling through the asteroid belt for about two months before it reached Gaspra. Galileo was 990 miles (1,593 kilometers) away from Gaspra when it whizzed by, and it was travelling at a relative speed of about 5 miles (8 km) per second. The spacecraft took several photos of the asteroid and used an instrument called the Near-Infrared Mapping Spectrometer to study its chemical composition and other physical properties. Galileo determined that Gaspra has an irregular and elongated shape measuring about 12 miles long and 7 miles wide. The images revealed that Gaspra was also covered in craters. Because Galileo was too far away for Gaspra's gravity to affect it, the spacecraft was not able to determine the asteroid's mass. A closeup view of asteroid Gaspra from NASA's Galileo spacecraft, which flew by the asteroid on the way to Jupiter. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Why it mattered The Galileo spacecraft's flyby of Gaspra was a pitstop near the midpoint of its 6-year journey to Jupiter, the largest planet in our solar system. NASA launched Galileo toward Jupiter in October 1989, with the probe swinging by Venus and Earth in 1990 before its encounter with Gaspra. The Gaspra flyby was the first asteroid flyby in history, with Galileo approaching to just under 1,000 miles (1,601 kilometers) while flying at a whopping 18,000 mph. Galileo's photos of Gaspra "revealed a cratered, complex, irregular body about 20 by 12 by 11 kilometers (12.4 by 7.4 by 6.8 miles), with a thin covering of dust and rubble," NASA wrote in an overview . "The picture we get of Gaspra is one of something that has suffered a lot during its history," the UPI press service quoted Joseph Veverka, a Galileo imaging team member, as saying at the time . "We suspect that this is the survivor of a series of catastrophic collisions in the past." An artist's conception of the Galileo spacecraft, which was launched in 1989 for a mission to Jupiter. (Image credit: NASA) Galileo would go on to fly by Earth a second time in 1992, then swing close by the asteroid Ida in 1993 before finally arriving at Jupiter in 1995. Along the way, the probe was in the right place at the right time to watch as the Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 broke into pieces and crashed into Jupiter in July 1994. Since Galileo's historic first asteroid flyby, NASA and other space agencies have gone on to land on asteroids (like NEAR on asteroid Eros ), collect samples of asteroids and return them to Earth (like NASA's OSIRIS-REx and Japan's Hayabusa probes), and have even intentionally crashed probes into asteroids (like NASA's DART asteroid impact mission ) to test planetary protection techniques. item.title: [VIDEO] Presidency: ‘We Can’t Do A Four-Year Gambling,’ Okorocha Faults Obi’s One-Term Promise
item.description: Former Imo State governor, Rochas Okorocha, has faulted the four-year presidency proposed by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, describing it as a gamble. Okorocha stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday. According to him, the South East must learn to be strategic in alliances. While drumming up support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, the former lawmaker representing Imo West said Tinubu has done no wrong to any Igbo man. item.title: FROM DRY TAPS TO RUNNING WATER: GOVERNOR ABBA KABIR YUSUF’S WATER LEGACY
item.description: By Farida Usman For generations, reliable public water supply has remained one of Kano’s most persistent development challenges. Across the ancient city, surrounding communities and expanding residential layouts, households have endured irregular supply, long searches for water and the uncertainty of when their taps would run again. For many residents, access to water became a daily struggle rather than a basic public service. That reality is beginning to change under Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, as the state’s water infrastructure rehabilitation moves from construction to service delivery; With the Challawa and Tamburawa treatment plants and their pumping stations reported to be 100 per cent complete, a successful test run conducted and water flow commenced, Kano has reached a significant milestone in its effort to restore dependable public water supply and its system. The achievement is important, but its real value lies in what it means for ordinary Bakano. Water must not merely be treated and pumped; it must reach homes, schools, hospitals, markets and businesses consistently. The administration’s next task is therefore to translate restored infrastructure into reliable and consistent supply across the communities that depend on it. Significantly, the test run has exposed reticulation challenges in parts of the distribution network across many locations in the state due to non-use of the pipes. These are now being addressed. Rather than diminishing the achievement, identifying these gaps provides a practical basis for targeted repairs and improvements. The ultimate measure of success will be how effectively the government closes these gaps and extends the benefits of the restored facilities to underserved neighbourhoods and communities. For communities such as Dukawa, Kofar Wambai and Shehi, as well as semi-urban settlements and newer layouts around Tamburawa, the expectation is clear: water should flow reliably, safely and affordably. Completing treatment plants is a major step; ensuring that the distribution network delivers their output to the intended users is the test that follows. The benefits of dependable water supply reach far beyond household convenience. Children can spend less time fetching water and more time learning. Families can reduce their reliance on costly alternatives, health facilities can improve hygiene, and small businesses can operate with fewer interruptions. item.content:encoded: By Farida Usman For generations, reliable public water supply has remained one of Kano’s most persistent development challenges. Across the ancient city, surrounding communities and expanding residential layouts, households have endured irregular supply, long searches for water and the uncertainty of when their taps would run again. For many residents, access to water became a daily struggle rather than a basic public service. That reality is beginning to change under Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, as the state’s water infrastructure rehabilitation moves from construction to service delivery; With the Challawa and Tamburawa treatment plants and their pumping stations reported to be 100 per cent complete, a successful test run conducted and water flow commenced, Kano has reached a significant milestone in its effort to restore dependable public water supply and its system. The achievement is important, but its real value lies in what it means for ordinary Bakano. Water must not merely be treated and pumped; it must reach homes, schools, hospitals, markets and businesses consistently. The administration’s next task is therefore to translate restored infrastructure into reliable and consistent supply across the communities that depend on it. Significantly, the test run has exposed reticulation challenges in parts of the distribution network across many locations in the state due to non-use of the pipes. These are now being addressed. Rather than diminishing the achievement, identifying these gaps provides a practical basis for targeted repairs and improvements. The ultimate measure of success will be how effectively the government closes these gaps and extends the benefits of the restored facilities to underserved neighbourhoods and communities. For communities such as Dukawa, Kofar Wambai and Shehi, as well as semi-urban settlements and newer layouts around Tamburawa, the expectation is clear: water should flow reliably, safely and affordably. Completing treatment plants is a major step; ensuring that the distribution network delivers their output to the intended users is the test that follows. The benefits of dependable water supply reach far beyond household convenience. Children can spend less time fetching water and more time learning. Families can reduce their reliance on costly alternatives, health facilities can improve hygiene, and small businesses can operate with fewer interruptions. Investment in water is therefore an investment in public health, education, productivity and human dignity and prosperity. sacrosanct, the restoration of infrastructure must not be mistaken for the complete resolution of Kano’s water challenges. The state’s growing population, expanding urban settlements and the continuing cost of operating and maintaining major facilities demand sustained attention. Hence, regular equipment maintenance, water-quality monitoring, timely pipeline repairs and transparent reporting on service delivery will be essential to prevent a return to the shortages that residents have unnecessarily endured for years. This is where the question of sustainability beyond 2031 becomes critical. Water infrastructure is a long-term public asset, not a temporary political project as always opined by Governor Abba. Its benefits must survive changes in government. The Yusuf administration is therefore establishing a durable maintenance system, securing a predictable operational funding, strengthening technical capacity and ensuring that future governments inherit functioning facilities rather than infrastructure requiring another round of rehabilitation. Citizens, too, have a pivotal role to play by protecting public pipelines, boreholes and other facilities against vandalism and misuse. But public participation must complement, not replace, the government’s responsibility to maintain infrastructure and provide transparent, accountable service. Ultimately, government performance is measured not by projects completed on paper but by improvements in people’s daily lives as we have seen in many sectors. Kano’s water intervention will be judged by the households receiving dependable supplies today and by whether that service continues in the years ahead and decades to come. The journey from dry taps to running water has begun. The task now is to close the remaining distribution gaps, sustain the momentum beyond 2031 and make reliable water supply a lasting reality for every community. That is a legacy worth building by the governor and a promise worthy of Kano First. -Farida Usman wrote in from Kano. She can be reached at fareederhtofa@gmail.com.

item.title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
item.description: Inter and AC Milan unveiled their new “Generali Stadium” Thursday, which will replace the iconic San Siro stadium from the 2031/32 season. It will be shaped “low in the body, and it rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said during a press conference in Milan. The design aims to bring spectators as close to the pitch as possible, with the stands behind the goals set at a steep 37-degree incline, said David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project. “The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling,” he said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling, and everything that we needed to do here was to carry it into the (new) building”. Manica said the design team “started with proximity”. “We brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass,” he said. They also paid great attention to acoustics: the roof covers the stands, leaving only the pitch exposed, and is designed to “amplify the roar” of the fans, Manica said. “This building is steeper than many other new buildings are built today, and that’s intentional, because it allows us to bring those seats up and over the field as much as possible, and create that sense of intimacy and atmosphere,” he said. The stadium, sponsored by the Italian insurance giant Generali, will also be capable of hosting American football games, rugby matches and concerts. “I want the crowd to come to the new stadium and to feel that excitement that they felt before, and to feel the building, living and breathing with them as it does currently,” Manica said. AC Milan and Inter paid 197 million euros ($219 million) to acquire the current stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they intend to build their new, shared home. The project for the new San Siro — which will have a capacity of 71,500 seats, compared to the current 75,000 — will cost the two clubs 1.2 billion euros. Construction is set to begin in 2028. Foster and Manica previously worked together on London’s Wembley Stadium. Milan’s current stadium — one of the most iconic in European football and often likened to a “concrete cathedral” — is the largest in Italy. But the venue, which opened in 1926, no longer meets the needs of spectators or the clubs, despite undergoing several renovations over the decades. San Siro, also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, will be largely demolished once construction work on the new stadium nears completion. The post Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ECB President Lagarde steps down in order to speak out
item.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down from her post several months early, in order to have more "freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy." The comments will fuel speculation about her future plans, ahead of a presidential election in her native France. The resignation also sparks a succession race, as Europe faces a turbulent fiscal future. Also in the show - oil giant TotalEnergies reports record profits as the EU warns on household energy bills.

item.title: Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman named deputy director for NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory
item.description: null The leader of NASA's first mission around the moon in half a century is the last to announce what's next for him after retiring from active astronaut duty. All four astronauts of the Artemis II mission, which flew around the moon in April, have hung up their spacesuits and moved on to greener pastures. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), managed by Caltech, announced yesterday that former NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman will step into the role of Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of JPL, beginning Nov. 30. "Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a JPL press release . Wiseman announced his transition to "astronaut emeritus" alongside Artemis II pilot Victor Glover in September. Glover, subsequently, accepted a full-time role as executive advisor to the president of his alma mater , California Polytechnic State University (Cal Poly). Artemis II mission specialists, Christina Koch and Canada's Jeremy Hansen , also made the decision to step away from their spaceflight careers. Hansen announced his career change in July, and has since entered into reservist duty with the Royal Canadian Air Force. Koch, more recently, was appointed as NASA's acting deputy chief engineer, effective Nov. 1. The quartet launched aboard NASA's Orion capsule on April 1, and completed a 10-day flight around the far side of the moon and back. Their mission took them further from Earth than any crewed spaceflight in history, and captured the attention of millions, who were captivated by the astronauts' incredible views and their ability to demonstrate the best traits of humanity, even while being the four people farthest from it. The mission served as a stepping stone in NASA's Artemis program which aims to return astronauts to the surface of the moon and eventually establish a permanent base there. NASA is targeting mid-2027 for Artemis III as a flight test with Orion and the two Artemis lunar lander spacecraft (SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon ). If everything goes according to plan, that mission will pave the way for Artemis IV, and the program's first crewed lunar landing in 2028. From left: The Artemis II crew — NASA astronaut Christina Koch, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, and NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover — take time out for a group hug inside the Orion spacecraft on April 6, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) A Baltimore native, Wiseman is a retired U.S. Navy captain who served as an aviator and test pilot before joining NASA's astronaut corps in 2009. He launched to space for the first time on the on the Soyuz TMA-13M mission to the International Space Station (ISS). item.content:encoded: null The leader of NASA's first mission around the moon in half a century is the last to announce what's next for him after retiring from active astronaut duty. All four astronauts of the Artemis II mission, which flew around the moon in April, have hung up their spacesuits and moved on to greener pastures. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), managed by Caltech, announced yesterday that former NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman will step into the role of Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of JPL, beginning Nov. 30. "Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a JPL press release . Wiseman announced his transition to "astronaut emeritus" alongside Artemis II pilot Victor Glover in September. Glover, subsequently, accepted a full-time role as executive advisor to the president of his alma mater , California Polytechnic State University (Cal Poly). Artemis II mission specialists, Christina Koch and Canada's Jeremy Hansen , also made the decision to step away from their spaceflight careers. Hansen announced his career change in July, and has since entered into reservist duty with the Royal Canadian Air Force. Koch, more recently, was appointed as NASA's acting deputy chief engineer, effective Nov. 1. The quartet launched aboard NASA's Orion capsule on April 1, and completed a 10-day flight around the far side of the moon and back. Their mission took them further from Earth than any crewed spaceflight in history, and captured the attention of millions, who were captivated by the astronauts' incredible views and their ability to demonstrate the best traits of humanity, even while being the four people farthest from it. The mission served as a stepping stone in NASA's Artemis program which aims to return astronauts to the surface of the moon and eventually establish a permanent base there. NASA is targeting mid-2027 for Artemis III as a flight test with Orion and the two Artemis lunar lander spacecraft (SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon ). If everything goes according to plan, that mission will pave the way for Artemis IV, and the program's first crewed lunar landing in 2028. From left: The Artemis II crew — NASA astronaut Christina Koch, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, and NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover — take time out for a group hug inside the Orion spacecraft on April 6, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) A Baltimore native, Wiseman is a retired U.S. Navy captain who served as an aviator and test pilot before joining NASA's astronaut corps in 2009. He launched to space for the first time on the on the Soyuz TMA-13M mission to the International Space Station (ISS). He spent 165 days in orbit serving as part of ISS Expeditions 40 and 41, and completed two spacewalks totaling nearly 13 hours. Before his selection for Artemis II, Wiseman worked as NASA's chief astronaut, overseeing crew readiness, astronaut assignments and flight safety from Dec. 2020 - Nov. 2022. As JPL's new deputy director, Wiseman will serve under Director Dave Gallagher, helping oversee "strategic leadership, stewardship, and continuous improvement of laboratory operations," according to the JPL release. JPL is a federally funded research and development center specializing in robotic space exploration. The lab is responsible for some of NASA's most recognizable planetary missions, including the Perseverance and Curiosity Mars rovers, Europa Clipper and the Voyager probes. JPL also operates NASA's Deep Space Network, which provides continuous communications with spacecraft throughout the solar system. "I've explored the furthest reaches of what a human can explore at NASA — and there were truly no words in the English vocabulary to describe seeing the sun disappear behind the moon from deep space," Wiseman said. "But that experience was really the jumping off point to go do the impossible things that Caltech and JPL dream, dare together, and do for NASA and the nation.”

item.title: 2027: INEC grants provisional clearance to Pantami, Gwarzo – Source
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night. In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night. INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections. The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome. The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29. Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates. item.title: Ubisoft Issues Official Update on Fate of Future Assassin's Creed Remakes
item.description: Ubisoft's latest Assassin's Creed game was a blast from the past. Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a remake of the 2013 pirate adventure. As remakes become more and more common in the industry, fans have naturally wondered if more Assassin's Creed remakes are in the pipeline. In 2024, CEO Yves Guillemot hinted at such , saying, "Players can be excited about some remakes, which will allow us to revisit some of the games we've created in the past and modernize them."

item.title: ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at the age of 86, an official statement said Thursday. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said. The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before crossing the Atlantic to enjoy an acclaimed career on the US stage and screen. His best known Hollywood roles were as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films. “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.” AFP The post ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The President landed at the King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, on Thursday night. ﻿ He was received by the Nigerian ambassador to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi’s head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir. Tinubu is in the country to perform Umrah, an Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. He departed Abuja for Makkah on Thursday afternoon. The event is an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for the nation’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress, Tinubu’s media aide, Bayo Onanuga, said in a statement on Wednesday. item.title: Troops neutralise two high-profile ISWAP leaders, others in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The troops of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have killed 15 Boko Haram terrorists, including two (2) prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira in Kerenoa, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State. This is as the Theatre Commander of OPHK, Major General Ibikunle Ajose on Thursday commissioned the newly constructed three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s one year in office, which also reflects his commitment to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. In a press statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni on Thursday said: “Troops of OPHK continued to record operational successes through sustained intelligence-led offensive operations aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and dismantling their networks across the theatre. “In a further operation, OPHK air assets, at about 9:20 pm on 28 October 2026, conducted an armed reconnaissance and air interdiction mission in the Kerenoa Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, resulting in the neutralisation of 15 terrorists and the destruction of an IED hideout. “The mission followed intelligence reports on terrorist activities in the area. During the operation, the air assets tracked two terrorists on a motorcycle to a makeshift structure beneath a tree. Further surveillance revealed additional movements around the location, indicating the presence of other terrorists. Consequently, the location was engaged with precision strikes. “Following the strikes, Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) indicated that 15 terrorists were neutralised, while structures at the location were destroyed. Additionally, a secondary fire observed after the engagement suggested that the targeted structure may have been used for the storage of terrorist IED logistics hub. “It has been confirmed that 2 prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira were amongst those neutralised while several other fighters were severely wounded, including the Wali (ISWAP Governor) of the area who is reported to be critically injured. “The operation forms part of OPHK’s sustained intelligence-led air offensive aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities, disrupting their hideouts and dismantling logistics networks across the theatre. The Joint Task Force continues to conduct coordinated operations against terrorist elements in the North East to achieve its Operational mandate of restoring total and long-lasting peace in the region,” Goni stated. Meanwhile, the Nigerian Army has reaffirmed its commitment to personnel welfare with the commissioning of three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maidugur
